### [Because I Got High](https://substack.com/redirect/1e7960d7-967f-4e72-b1da-566463eddacb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
But so what if people are smoking more weed? The common narrative today is certainly that pot is healthier than alcohol. Isn't this a good shift? After all, the pro-weed advocacy group NORML says that "[marijuana is not addictive](https://substack.com/redirect/6cc552a3-6d36-47a2-8684-80feec42aea5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)."
This is, to use the technical term, [horseshit](https://substack.com/redirect/efc79115-a047-4c83-a4f2-1b6b5940bb53?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
For starters, **marijuana use among teenagers is linked to[poorer school performance, lower long-term socioeconomic attainment](https://substack.com/redirect/419b994e-66e3-4921-9fea-00a18016746f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), and [higher rates of psychosis](https://substack.com/redirect/51390c2e-0a17-4a95-8b1b-8af0e993f85e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**.
It may well be the case that marijuana is less bad for you than alcohol, but the number of people with [marijuana use disorders is in the tens of millions](https://substack.com/redirect/40b59ace-7599-4a66-b012-48d683803235?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)--higher than the number suffering other afflictions you might think would outrank problematic weed consumption.12
Finally, and this may be obvious, but [studies very consistently find](https://substack.com/redirect/b9c74712-f4cf-44ab-88ba-f439dfdb830a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that the higher the THC concentration in people's marijuana, the higher their rates of [cannabis use disorder](https://substack.com/redirect/018e6c85-1859-48fe-96fb-92d359fd7995?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and psychosis.
As products become more and more potent, in part because more consumers have built up tolerances to [lower-THC products](https://substack.com/redirect/9a2120af-fc0e-4f1f-ae7b-ecccf1d9d4be?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), that's a real issue.
### [Roll Me Up](https://substack.com/redirect/1cf18199-9235-4fb2-9437-e84bf1719569?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
I don't think marijuana should be illegal. I think the opposite--it's time for the federal government to legalize pot.
Why? Because right now, the federal government is caught in purgatory: they don't really enforce laws on the books, but because it's illegal, they're effectively toothless in regulating marijuana consumption, marijuana growers, and marijuana distributors.
That's clearly not working; marijuana use is being governed by patchwork and often inadequate state-level laws. Without intervention, these problems will only become more acute.
Americans everywhere should have consistent laws that govern marijuana use, which should include:
1. **A cap on THC levels**. Vapes that have 90% THC concentration are dangerous and addictive, especially for young adults. There's no need for that level of concentration in marijuana products.
2. **Tax rates based on THC rates, not just "is it marijuana or isn't it."** [Illinois does this now](https://substack.com/redirect/c0a43f58-3128-4148-9474-3fd4089ba7e4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg); most other states don't.13 But a 3% THC joint and a 90% THC vape aren't the same product, and they shouldn't be treated as such.
3. **Better education and information**. Everyone understands that drinking a 12 oz. glass of Bud Light isn't the same as drinking a 12 oz. glass of whiskey. There isn't that awareness among the public about marijuana, even though THC levels from one product to another can vary even more drastically than that.
4. **Clear and uniform labeling** , so people know what they're buying and consuming. This exists with alcohol products already.
5. **Better research**. Driving-while-high rates, for instance, are [very likely going up](https://substack.com/redirect/dfbff1e3-4df2-43cb-8618-0a0b46fc82c0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). But research is surprisingly scant, and that makes it hard to really figure out prevalence and the right policy interventions. (Yes, [driving while high is dangerous](https://substack.com/redirect/44e2e724-e71f-414a-b976-5f36e6535cda?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).)

As marijuana rapidly becomes more potent, Americans have inadvertently legalized what is effectively a new drug. Regulation--at the state level and at the federal level--needs to catch up.

Regulation hasn't caught up. | | | Oct 7 | | | | | | | | | | Perhaps the single biggest shift in public opinion in my lifetime has been support for legalized marijuana.1 The idea that not only would there be legal weed, but also that you could buy it in clean, above-board retail shops is a crazy development from where the country was in 2000.2 A quarter-century ago, I truly think that only the hardcore stoners and hippies would've really believed that this was possible. I've never had super hardened views on legalized pot.3 I , but that was more on technical grounds; I thought (and still think) that the amendment was poorly written. Nonetheless, I agree that no one should be put in jail for smoking weed. In any event, that's a false narrative; for true marijuana-specific offenses to begin with, even though recreational weed is . But one thing that's been lost in the (largely settled) debate about legalizing weed: today's marijuana is nothing like the marijuana from a generation ago. Because of how marijuana has been grown and bred, than it was back in 1977, pre-legalization. Arguments in favor of legalizing pot focus on a drug that isn't particularly strong and isn't particularly dangerous. As it gets stronger and more potent, that's not obviously true anymore. Regulators need to catch up. Article summary: Marijuana has become much more potent, even since states have legalized it. Yes, marijuana is addicting. Especially at high potencies, that 's a particular concern for teenagers and for daily users. The solution? The federal government should finally legalize it, because that would allow for better, more consistent regulation and consumer protection. ? Let's start with the math: weed is getting really, really powerful. This is a chart from the Drug Enforcement Administration: | | ---|---|--- Source: DEA, Keep in mind that this is the average ; there's a lot of pot out there that's even stronger. There are marijuana products where the , especially with . As more states move towards legalization--either full recreational legalization or medical legalization, which is being sold.5 Because this is regulated at the state level, how this is communicated to consumers varies considerably.6 The other thing that's alarming about this increase is that when people support legalization, as the nature of marijuana changes, it's not obvious that they really know what they're voting to legalize. A joint with low THC concentration is very different from a vape whose THC concentration might be 25× higher. Here's what I mean: at some point in their lifetime, but only 21% have done so in the past year. That leaves 26% of Americans--some 75 million people7--who have consumed marijuana, and who therefore think they understand what's being sold at the local vape shop, without necessarily understanding how much more potent it's become. At the same time that marijuana is becoming way more potent, it's also becoming way more common. A few years ago, for the first time ever, the number of people who consume marijuana every day surpassed the number who drink every day.8 | | ---|---|--- Source: I've brought this up before in the too: when you legalize something, more people are going to do it. Yes, plenty of people partake in all sorts of illegal activities, but a lot of people don't really want to break the law. That's backed up by the data here: adults in states where marijuana is legal than in states where it's not.9 The other evidence comes from global marijuana consumption. It turns out that North America is unusual in having legalized weed; in . The consequences of that are borne out in the data, where North America's rates of marijuana consumption are by far the highest in the world: | | ---|---|--- Source: The common narrative these days, shared by and alike, is that Gen Z doesn't drink alcohol and they consume weed instead.10 That's not really accurate. It is true that than in the past. But unlike adults in America, kids are also consuming less marijuana. It's just a slower rate of decline: | | ---|---|--- Source: This data masks an alarming underlying trend, however. While the number of 12th graders consuming marijuana is down over the past 30 years, the number who consume marijuana every day is actually up : | | ---|---|--- Source: , p. 369 This trend we're seeing here--that a greater share of 12th graders are using every day--is not the case with alcohol. In the past 30 years, the has fallen 74%.11 This, combined with kids being exposed to higher-THC products at a younger age, seems concerning. But so what if people are smoking more weed? The common narrative today is certainly that pot is healthier than alcohol. Isn't this a good shift? After all, the pro-weed advocacy group NORML says that "." This is, to use the technical term, . For starters, marijuana use among teenagers is linked to, and . It may well be the case that marijuana is less bad for you than alcohol, but the number of people with than the number suffering other afflictions you might think would outrank problematic weed consumption.12 Finally, and this may be obvious, but that the higher the THC concentration in people's marijuana, the higher their rates of and psychosis. As products become more and more potent, in part because more consumers have built up tolerances to , that's a real issue. I don't think marijuana should be illegal. I think the opposite--it's time for the federal government to legalize pot. Why? Because right now, the federal government is caught in purgatory: they don't really enforce laws on the books, but because it's illegal, they're effectively toothless in regulating marijuana consumption, marijuana growers, and marijuana distributors. That's clearly not working; marijuana use is being governed by patchwork and often inadequate state-level laws. Without intervention, these problems will only become more acute. Americans everywhere should have consistent laws that govern marijuana use, which should include: 1. A cap on THC levels. Vapes that have 90% THC concentration are dangerous and addictive, especially for young adults. There's no need for that level of concentration in marijuana products. 2. Tax rates based on THC rates, not just "is it marijuana or isn't it." ; most other states don't.13 But a 3% THC joint and a 90% THC vape aren't the same product, and they shouldn't be treated as such. 3. Better education and information. Everyone understands that drinking a 12 oz. glass of Bud Light isn't the same as drinking a 12 oz. glass of whiskey. There isn't that awareness among the public about marijuana, even though THC levels from one product to another can vary even more drastically than that. 4. Clear and uniform labeling , so people know what they're buying and consuming. This exists with alcohol products already. 5. Better research. Driving-while-high rates, for instance, are . But research is surprisingly scant, and that makes it hard to really figure out prevalence and the right policy interventions. (Yes, .) As marijuana rapidly becomes more potent, Americans have inadvertently legalized what is effectively a new drug. Regulation--at the state level and at the federal level--needs to catch up. ? As a 30-year prosecutor, I have prosecuted thousands of sex crimes. including trafficking. My work and passion for standing up for victims has been recognized by the Crime Victims Foundation and I have overseen human trafficking cases as Eaton County Prosecutor.
That's why it was so disturbing for me to hear that these survivors begged my opponent to not legalize prostitution in Washtenaw County because it would send a clear message to traffickers that Washtenaw was open for business.
One of the survivors, Leyna, said that's exactly what the FBI has seen. Traffickers are openly talking about how they can operate in Washtenaw without being prosecuted.

|
# PRESS RELEASE

**FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE**
October 7, 2026

**CONTACT**
Todd Cheewing
Todd@Ascent-Strategic.com

**LILY TANG WILLIAMS HITS THE AIRWAVES WITH NEW ADS AS CAMPAIGN ENTERS HOME STRETCH**

WEARE, N.H. — Lily Tang Williams is taking her message directly to Granite Staters’ TVs and devices, launching two new ads that sharpen her home-stretch contrast with Maggie Goodlander and the Washington establishment on affordability, freedom, and the American Dream. The first spot, [_Make the American Dream Affordable_](https://us.list-manage.com/ICtIaRysQ8N?e=c338950e03&c2id=adf8b61e01be85c238f26a96cfd7c41c), tells Lily’s story of growing up under Mao’s communist regime and coming to America in search of freedom and opportunity. Against stark images of communist China and Lily’s life today, the ad warns against collectivism and promises Lily will fight for a more affordable life for Granite Staters. “I lived under communism. I saw firsthand where it leads: poverty, despair and the loss of individual freedom,” said Williams. “I came to America because here, hard work and freedom give people the opportunity to build a better life. I will fight to make sure we never lose that American Dream.” The second spot, [_Complaints Department_](https://us.list-manage.com/6H7ydIpXbld?e=c338950e03&c2id=adf8b61e01be85c238f26a96cfd7c41c), takes aim at the affordability crisis. Lily sits behind a literal complaints desk as the ad highlights rising healthcare costs and Washington’s failure to deliver relief — closing with a simple message: “NEW HAMPSHIRE CAN’T AFFORD MORE GOODLANDER.”
**VIEW THE ADS HERE (CLICK LINKS**) [Make the American Dream Affordable](https://us.list-manage.com/hHtTNQvE930?e=c338950e03&c2id=adf8b61e01be85c238f26a96cfd7c41c)
[Complaints Department](https://us.list-manage.com/pUwq94PR3Ry?e=c338950e03&c2id=adf8b61e01be85c238f26a96cfd7c41c)
“Granite Staters have one big complaint: life costs too much,” said Williams. “Maggie Goodlander and the Washington establishment aren’t fixing it. New Hampshire can’t afford more of the same.” The six-figure broadcast and digital push marks a major home-stretch escalation for Williams, taking her campaign’s defining message — freedom, affordability, and preserving the American Dream — directly to voters across the district.

**About Lily Tang Williams**
Born in China just before Mao’s Cultural Revolution to working-class parents, Lily Tang Williams immigrated to the United States with nothing and built a life as an entrepreneur, educator, and community leader in Weare, NH. A living embodiment of the American Dream, she brings a uniquely powerful perspective to the fight for freedom and limited government.

In 2024, Williams won the Republican nomination and captured 47% of the general election vote against current incumbent Maggie Goodlander — coming closer than any Republican has in more than a decade to flipping NH-02. She is back and running stronger than ever in 2026.

| Friend, Defend Our Courts has been sounding the alarm about Trump’s plot to rig elections since our founding in Spring 2025. In our first major race, the ‘25 Pennsylvania Supreme Court election, we laid out the stakes for Democrats: Trump is attempting to take control of PA state Supreme Court so that he will have control over the court with final say on election related matters in the most important swing state in America. In short, we’ve been warning that Trump is trying to control how states run their elections by planting his loyalist judges on State Supreme Courts. Our critics called us “alarmist.” MAGA called us crazy. But what Donald Trump announced proves without a doubt that the plot we have been warning about is very, very real:

Trump is now openly declaring his war on free and fair elections. In the Constitution, it clearly outlines that state governments, not the federal government, have responsibility for how elections are administered. It’s literally in the first Article of the Constitution. And that means there’s good news and bad news: The good news: Trump’s call to nationalize elections is so unconstitutional that even the MAGA controlled Supreme Court is unlikely to allow it. The bad news: Now that Trump has publicly stated his end goal, MAGA’s going to go nuclear to try and take control of state Supreme Courts across the country. Defend Our Court’s mission has never been more essential to preserving Democracy than it is now. In 2026, there are state Supreme Court elections in several key swing states; Georgia, Michigan, and Wisconsin. Defend Our Courts helped spearhead the defense of PA’s state Supreme Court. And Democrats there didn’t just win, they won massive 30+ point landslides. In Philadelphia where we concentrated the majority of our efforts, turnout surged by 34 percent. That was the largest increase in the state. And it made the difference. Now we’re taking our winning formula and our army of over 100k grassroots supporters to battle MAGA in GA, MI, and WI in 2026. With the national party stretched thin with House and Senate races, our role will be crucial in saving democracy. I was a junior in high school on 9/11. The next day, I began my West Point application. After graduating, I did six overseas deployments serving in Iraq and Afghanistan. I did that out of a love for this country. Peter, my name is Cait Conley and I’m the Democratic nominee to flip NY-17. Back then, I never thought that the greatest threat to our nation would come from within our own borders. But the people running this administration do not share our values—or the values of the generations of Americans who fought and sacrificed to make this country better. So I made the decision to run for Congress, again, out of love for this country. **My campaign’s final public FEC deadline is a week from today. After this deadline, our team has to report how much we’ve raised, and from how many donors.** Mike Lawler has been outspending us on TV, and outside money is flooding into this district to help him. Elon Musk and Donald Trump are both spending big on his behalf. When this report comes out, we need to be able to show that we have the resources to push back against their attacks AND fuel our on-the-ground voter outreach program. But New York is the single most expensive place in the country to run a political campaign. The only way we’re going to afford this sort of operation is with your help. So please. [**I am humbly asking you to chip in $10 or $17 to help us beat Mike Lawler. Have you marked your calendars yet?
In less than one month, we'll know the outcome of this election. And in just 8 days, folks will start casting ballots in person during early voting. I need your help to reach them before then.
**[Time's running out to spread our message and impact the outcome of this race, so I'm personally asking you to pitch in $5 or whatever you can to my campaign today.](https://substack.com/redirect/7f882ce8-4cf8-43ed-a0f6-2db75378b287?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
[Donate](https://substack.com/redirect/7f882ce8-4cf8-43ed-a0f6-2db75378b287?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
From the get-go, national Republicans made it clear they were ready to open their wallets and make this one of the most expensive Senate races of the cycle.
14 months and tens of millions of dollars later, they made good on that promise, and it's no secret as to why:
Experts say our campaign could flip North Carolina's U.S. Senate seat blue for the first time since 2008. That's good news, because we have to win here to have any chance of taking back the Senate majority.
I've won tough statewide campaigns here in North Carolina before, and the only way I'll do it again in less than a month from now is if grassroots supporters like you power us to victory.
So before North Carolinians start heading to early voting sites, we need to be ready. We need to head into these final four weeks with the momentum and resources to take on everything MAGA throws our way.
Hundreds of thousands of folks have contributed already. Now, I'm asking you to join them and know that you've done all you can to wake up on November 4th with a Democratic Senate.
**[So please, will you pitch in whatever fits in your budget- whether it's $5 or $10 - to help us cross the finish line in North Carolina and take back the Senate for Democrats?](https://substack.com/redirect/7f882ce8-4cf8-43ed-a0f6-2db75378b287?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**

Let's win this thing.
Roy Cooper

Team,
Senator Reverend Raphael Warnock here.
**I’m reaching out because I’m proud to support my friend Chris Pappas for the United States Senate in New Hampshire.**
I’ve been through a few tough elections myself, so I know how important it is to have people in your corner when the stakes are high.
And Chris needs that support.
Republicans and their allies are putting a tremendous amount of money into this race because they know how important this Senate seat is. In fact they’re already pouring over $50 million dollars into cementing their majority.
**That’s a lot of money to go up against.[So I’m asking: Will you chip in $5 or whatever you can afford today to help Chris Pappas compete and win in New Hampshire?](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20261007_1.0xP6O6&refcode=em20261007-1&t=2&akid=9377%2E582294%2EiTtJK8)**
**[Donate $5 »](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20261007_1.0xP6O6&amount=5&refcode=em20261007-1&t=21&akid=9377%2E582294%2EiTtJK8)**
Chris knows he won’t have the billionaires’ outside spending groups on his side. What he does have is a grassroots team of people who believe in what he’s fighting for and are willing to show up.
**That’s how we won in Georgia.**
In both of my Senate races, I saw people who didn’t have millions of dollars to give decide that they were going to do what they could. They gave $5. They gave $25. They talked to their neighbors. They showed up. And when enough people do that together, it makes a big difference.
That’s the kind of grassroots support Chris needs right now in New Hampshire.
**[So I’m asking you personally: Will you chip in $5 or whatever you can today to help Chris Pappas win his Senate race?](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20261007_1.0xP6O6&refcode=em20261007-1&t=22&akid=9377%2E582294%2EiTtJK8)**

I’m proud to be supporting Chris, and I hope you’ll join me.
Thank you for all you do,
Raphael

The heavy thud of a lid and the receding roar of a truck signal a departure.
We are taught to believe in "away." We move our waste and our mistakes, and for a moment, they seem to vanish.
But away is not gone; it is simply elsewhere.
In a living system, nothing is truly discarded; it merely enters a new chain of consequence. The shortcut is not the disappearance of the burden, but its movement.
And whenever a burden is moved, a question remains: **Who receives it?**
The act of discarding solves a problem at one end while creating a responsibility at the other.
**Pause.
Breathe.
Look Deeper.**
**Refuel.**
**Welcome to Sweet Ground.**

Reflecting on the last three years. | | [ ](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.XaF8mXqsA6b2dSPmhsleMYE5U9NTRbOMLNsSMiwuHsSkvWspXpNzcqkzSIoupdDWkL2pjwIimGUsMZ1ZguqiawQwc8Iht3aCrkdXpsjBpSLw1ZyD5bxKE_JcgYrCqbqG6f6Js4eu-CjI10hbGycmMIVtCXbYptZQUjL2PbQJX3eoyZ1nbh6ft3fVVSTveML1oRSJECVMEcq5iYqz0lUz8QCHF-RxQ4jYGXAjKJDB64NIhHm7MWEWyx-ItZeCM_4YYxiZna7kdL0_LdTqXpTroKbeC2U_3JcrqZrF0d5NMUNf4ep56XASqVwCDaaKOQAU/4uo/6KJfNFg-S--1Ru_vYojNog/h0/h001.Z0Pb0hDTR-UUddlav6l2WscVS2b1Z1h6xy3Op5iqsx8)
---
Peter, There's a word weighing heavily on my mind today. One that has rung in my ears for many months - years now - and now has grown so urgent it demands to be spoken aloud. I'm talking about genocide. Three years ago today, a vicious attack on Israeli civilians shocked the world. As someone who is half-Jewish and signed up to serve after September 11th, I initially defended Israel's intense response to October 7th. Like many Americans, I understood the fear, grief, and determination to prevent another attack. But what has transpired over the course of the last three years is unconscionable, and I will not defend it. _I cannot._ Benjamin Netanyahu and his far right government have systematically laid waste to Gaza. Family homes, hospitals, schools and refugee camps have been targeted indiscriminately with heavy munitions. Over 70,000 are known to be dead in direct kinetic strikes. Countless more are buried in the rubble that is all that remains of most of Gaza. Even more have died of disease and treatable injuries stemming from a deliberate withholding of humanitarian aid and denial of medical care. Many many thousands of the victims of this widespread campaign of extermination are children. As a father, it is impossible not to see the faces of my own kids in the images that have poured forth from Gaza. The Israeli government has targeted journalists - including their families - to suppress the truth of what every major human rights organization and genocide scholar agrees is indisputably a genocide. But if there was a shred of doubt remaining, one need only look at the recently released satellite images revealing what little remains of Gaza. The team at Track AIPAC recently released a tool allowing you to explore the difference yourself, and I encourage everyone to take a look:
---
| [ ](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfqs6gc2C5hUDUAX_oNaSPVDobFeqfVfzIW2x4J26hzyt84qKPcrW90Va_ayZKdEattrJmh-i_gWN3LyEbtIgkpr4ozXw2sYX9Ue-c-OU3-aW6ukAvEUIDZfcIu8eme3jGIdGhqU89f8MZPHtJzkVPeR0jIrzET4igBy_YCzUDXgvpPwWXSpRNBYmaxTMkUdbufb5LIuVtYiKzq_kg0wzgvvRfODjrdZVJLHOGwmHYz6ZxNBRYDxCdjggLYxAfJS2oMMj-ewOQhpRNu4_eo-1aQYhP38oq3NTjsIAEqlYPF9vr-CdcPDbUPmJ4hfb3Wnjl0AO0RfQmwFMVgBpvqIMGA7CmtLl7pyB42Ei1-YdAJh1Aw/4uo/6KJfNFg-S--1Ru_vYojNog/h1/h001.aQYkVW6i5mGRKq_ztoFpQUWOc9DiImCdQwqJ7yfCr8c)
---
The piles of rubble you see there are all that remains of the most densely populated urban area in the world. Over 2 million people have been displaced or killed. Half of those displaced are children.
And it’s all happening thanks to the patronage of the United States.
For three years, our government – including my opponent Keith Self and hundreds of others in Congress – have gladly cashed checks from AIPAC and other pro-Israel lobby groups pushing to keep the bombs flowing.
---
| [ ](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfqs6gc2C5hUDUAX_oNaSPVDobFeqfVfzIW2x4J26hzyt84qKPcrW90Va_ayZKdEattokhwKK5X5m_XTKbNy8bdtHLZPrm0_OJlPLpChKDGYSYzM8OGTP-kBAXOKd9T9WxW7WMPiFeMe1RYrjaJTn2lQzEBZL50xGxaVGlIbRHIwa4ctYpcB_lMm_guo8oCJKvRr8WmPkCYbJ0TF0OvN-qna0d2BjhB5fs_m16pMCvUyobcTDB75l0MjsKpvhLwFzOzJ7e5Hfb7TqyPFd1nsqodPawlZVG4qY5KZT0QbjE6jXIb1icxMsiwwNAzH5sw4cg0M5gS6n-A4OfuD8_NQP461xza0jIeo_IIvt1eAx4vxt_g/4uo/6KJfNFg-S--1Ru_vYojNog/h2/h001.CXOh0rpUt2B7MlZE8VyLhRdmkJKkDevgjFJ62R4zDV8)
---
For Keith Self to take this money as a member of the House Foreign Affairs Committee is a gross conflict of interest.
But instead of defending our alliances and ensuring the president pursues diplomatic solutions before plunging us into another catastrophic war, he’s voted for every single weapons package to keep arming Netanyahu while he starves the children of Gaza and invades southern Lebanon.
I’ve never taken a dime from AIPAC or any foreign lobby group or corporate PAC, because I do not believe you can represent the will of the people when you’re on the payroll of special interests. I’m proud to be endorsed by Track AIPAC and will join with leaders like Rep. Delia Ramirez to pass human-centered legislation like Block the Bombs, as a start.
---
| [ ](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfqs6gc2C5hUDUAX_oNaSPVDobFeqfVfzIW2x4J26hzyt84qKPcrW90Va_ayZKdEatto5Q8NsEyD9jC9yjnlLHTJQosqPBTmIt2B62SpxBQXSqV2Mae3vPuJuo5DYjzpetk8oe1bqIkKCE8SFnrWcXNUpeGjJLUd6PaEzHghCPT4xWEbefqPFf81db7UNbAa6pA0OzgthvyESTZMwzkbygt6SSKFSKfcHfCdEHrRS4XTQmakVXwsgK5VsMlQkjmIhHqH6vmFFb0qqd9nTpmBqIch0SPHH_5TPnofZN6Hop7VSxMOv4mpoJwuVcceIN7khZ8qBsEUmKhFQao0AeN9Du95NI0g6zMGJfqM5StLSIPt1cQ/4uo/6KJfNFg-S--1Ru_vYojNog/h3/h001.FzNEw6K_FoblImSeTT4i6MBEMFRGg6V6ldv5rrOQ8uE)
---
My opponent spends his time in Congress reflexively defending everything Donald Trump does and promoting blatant anti-Muslim hatred with his “Sharia-Free America Caucus”.
Meanwhile he continues to supply the weapons and the political cover for a rogue foreign dictator engaged in what Amnesty International, Israeli human rights groups B’Tselem and Physicians for Human Rights-Israel, the UN’s independent Commission of Inquiry and the International Association of Genocide Scholars have all concluded is a genocide.
We’ve watched this play out for three long years. Despite a so-called ceasefire, the killing continues. The withholding of aid continues. The refusal to admit foreign journalists continues. The unjust imprisonment of notable Palestinian leaders – doctors, journalists, teachers – continues.
This is more than a deep humanitarian crisis. It is a moral crisis. And it must end.
American law is very clear. Any foreign security force suspected to be engaged in gross human rights abuses and war crimes cannot receive weapons from the United States government.
No exceptions.
Keith Self refuses to uphold our laws. I’m running for Congress to see that we do.
American power rests on more than weapons and wealth. It rests on credibility, partnerships and whether our word means anything. Alienating allies and excusing abuses leaves us with fewer partners, less influence and less ability to protect our interests.
The generation that fought fascism and survived the Holocaust understood the cost of a world ruled by “might makes right” instead of international law. They left us NATO and the UN.
My opponent is squandering that legacy every single day.
Winning this seat in November means an end to the hate, division, and chaos of Keith Self’s brand of politics. But more than that, it means one more vote to end these atrocities and literally save lives.
[If you’re with me, please consider a contribution to my campaign today. We have 27 days to pull this off, and we need everyone on board.](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfqs6gc2C5hUDUAX_oNaSPVDobFeqfVfzIW2x4J26hzyt84qKPcrW90Va_ayZKdEattqlf5PLqT0xD9l4hIKPfOxPseEjPfEfADmfxXFA-tNA6oB7JBH-8KuZnY_5514_ClW2NQchDwnBJXBekmAkgkRn6yxinnRR8RX8ZA3C71jyIundlQeZY8ca1Yn7vLjUlByyWD0X4bK1caWlhTofwtKHWAFU6lK9YdmvaCpk05Aafau6Sa9CeOZ6Lszvr5KJAJKusZ355kmeGQvC7MN8jFuxx6mP0WFpv1REXcGmxaKRWwY9-WF9HxuMcsOfhckwYtKiYTHTy0RAKIeIylB8672T5KHlbwHInqodFA_quwYkCQ/4uo/6KJfNFg-S--1Ru_vYojNog/h4/h001.dU9DD4HFMXyGQUuau0JQrhsM7B-BgVkOvPFNHKlLssY)

Evan Hunt Democratic Nominee TX-03

clean_body: Reflecting on the last three years. | | Peter, There's a word weighing heavily on my mind today. One that has rung in my ears for many months - years now - and now has grown so urgent it demands to be spoken aloud. I'm talking about genocide. Three years ago today, a vicious attack on Israeli civilians shocked the world. As someone who is half-Jewish and signed up to serve after September 11th, I initially defended Israel's intense response to October 7th. Like many Americans, I understood the fear, grief, and determination to prevent another attack. But what has transpired over the course of the last three years is unconscionable, and I will not defend it. I cannot. Benjamin Netanyahu and his far right government have systematically laid waste to Gaza. Family homes, hospitals, schools and refugee camps have been targeted indiscriminately with heavy munitions. Over 70,000 are known to be dead in direct kinetic strikes. Countless more are buried in the rubble that is all that remains of most of Gaza. Even more have died of disease and treatable injuries stemming from a deliberate withholding of humanitarian aid and denial of medical care. Many many thousands of the victims of this widespread campaign of extermination are children. As a father, it is impossible not to see the faces of my own kids in the images that have poured forth from Gaza. The Israeli government has targeted journalists - including their families - to suppress the truth of what every major human rights organization and genocide scholar agrees is indisputably a genocide. But if there was a shred of doubt remaining, one need only look at the recently released satellite images revealing what little remains of Gaza. The team at Track AIPAC recently released a tool allowing you to explore the difference yourself, and I encourage everyone to take a look: | The piles of rubble you see there are all that remains of the most densely populated urban area in the world. Over 2 million people have been displaced or killed. Half of those displaced are children. And it’s all happening thanks to the patronage of the United States. For three years, our government – including my opponent Keith Self and hundreds of others in Congress – have gladly cashed checks from AIPAC and other pro-Israel lobby groups pushing to keep the bombs flowing. | For Keith Self to take this money as a member of the House Foreign Affairs Committee is a gross conflict of interest. But instead of defending our alliances and ensuring the president pursues diplomatic solutions before plunging us into another catastrophic war, he’s voted for every single weapons package to keep arming Netanyahu while he starves the children of Gaza and invades southern Lebanon. I’ve never taken a dime from AIPAC or any foreign lobby group or corporate PAC, because I do not believe you can represent the will of the people when you’re on the payroll of special interests. I’m proud to be endorsed by Track AIPAC and will join with leaders like Rep. Delia Ramirez to pass human-centered legislation like Block the Bombs, as a start. | My opponent spends his time in Congress reflexively defending everything Donald Trump does and promoting blatant anti-Muslim hatred with his “Sharia-Free America Caucus”. Meanwhile he continues to supply the weapons and the political cover for a rogue foreign dictator engaged in what Amnesty International, Israeli human rights groups B’Tselem and Physicians for Human Rights-Israel, the UN’s independent Commission of Inquiry and the International Association of Genocide Scholars have all concluded is a genocide. We’ve watched this play out for three long years. Despite a so-called ceasefire, the killing continues. The withholding of aid continues. The refusal to admit foreign journalists continues. The unjust imprisonment of notable Palestinian leaders – doctors, journalists, teachers – continues. This is more than a deep humanitarian crisis. It is a moral crisis. And it must end. American law is very clear. Any foreign security force suspected to be engaged in gross human rights abuses and war crimes cannot receive weapons from the United States government. No exceptions. Keith Self refuses to uphold our laws. I’m running for Congress to see that we do. American power rests on more than weapons and wealth. It rests on credibility, partnerships and whether our word means anything. Alienating allies and excusing abuses leaves us with fewer partners, less influence and less ability to protect our interests. The generation that fought fascism and survived the Holocaust understood the cost of a world ruled by “might makes right” instead of international law. They left us NATO and the UN. My opponent is squandering that legacy every single day. Winning this seat in November means an end to the hate, division, and chaos of Keith Self’s brand of politics. But more than that, it means one more vote to end these atrocities and literally save lives. We can’t let all the rampant, unprecedented fraud that took place under her watch go unnoticed. It’s a national disgrace. That’s why Tim Walz was forced to end his re-election campaign... Meanwhile, his right hand wants to be our next U.S. Senator.

subject: FWD: More Hollywood donors line up for Annie Andrews
body:
Annie Andrews has Hollywood. I have you. |
Fellow Patriot - more Hollywood donors are lining up for my opponent.

This week, John Goodman sent out a fundraising text for my opponent.

# Palestine
* **Killed and wounded in Gaza:** Over the past 24 hours, five Palestinians were killed--four in new Israeli attacks and one due to wounds sustained in an earlier attack--and 11 injured across Gaza, according to the Palestinian Ministry of Health.
* The total recorded death toll since October 7, 2023 is now 74,250 killed, with 175,278 injured. Since October 11, 2025, the first full day of the so-called ceasefire, Israel has killed at least 1,467 Palestinians in Gaza and wounded 5,161, while 836 bodies have been recovered.

* **Israel continues to kill Palestinians in Gaza three years into the genocide:** Four Palestinians were [killed](https://substack.com/redirect/9f62f2b2-7c8d-45d7-b0e5-1d5653a59c04?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) by Israeli fire and strikes across the Gaza Strip since dawn on Wednesday, according to WAFA.
* A Palestinian Civil Defence member was shot and killed by Israeli forces during an attempt to evacuate people wounded in Jabalia.
* A young boy was shot and killed amid heavy Israeli fire east of Khan Younis.
* Another Palestinian was killed in an Israeli drone strike in Khan Younis, while a fourth was killed in an Israeli airstrike on a refugee camp in the city.
* **Palestinian killed, dozens detained as Israeli forces and settlers attack across the occupied West Bank:**
* **Nablus:** A 44-year-old Palestinian was killed and nine others wounded, one seriously, after Israeli settlers accompanied by Israeli forces [attacked](https://substack.com/redirect/2deb1fe4-8020-416f-9268-dfe7509d593c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) olive harvesters from Burqa in the Ramin plain between Nablus and Tulkarm on Wednesday, according to WAFA.
* Seven other Palestinians were injured after being beaten by Israeli forces in Nablus. Israeli forces also imposed a curfew on Nablus city, raided homes and detained several Palestinians, including journalist Umair Staitiyeh, while turning Karman School into a field interrogation center.
* In Al-Lubban Al-Sharqiya, settlers accompanied by Israeli forces erected dozens of Israeli flags between Palestinian homes and businesses.
* **Ramallah:** Israeli forces [imposed](https://substack.com/redirect/0f033af7-54ff-4140-98cc-ae2be7f61be6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a curfew on Burqa, east of Ramallah as settlers raided the village.
* In Al-Mughayyir, settlers attacked Palestinian homes and set fire to a vehicle belonging to foreign journalists who were in the village documenting Israeli and settler attacks.
* **Bethlehem:** Settlers accompanied by Israeli forces entered Palestinian farmland in Al-Minya, southeast of Bethlehem, and [stole](https://substack.com/redirect/1d053103-a10c-4bf3-ab31-8f13e346681e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) harvested olives. Landowners have reportedly been prevented from reaching their land for more than a month.
* **Jenin:** A Palestinian man was [shot and wounded](https://substack.com/redirect/581b9d0f-8de6-478e-8aa6-d3a5fcdbb0a9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) by Israeli forces during a raid in central Jenin. Israeli forces also closed several gates and roads across the governorate, raided homes, demolished a memorial in Ya'bad, and removed photographs of Palestinians killed by Israel.
* **East Jerusalem:** Israeli forces [carried out](https://substack.com/redirect/af0b0e8b-3450-460b-8251-7b0dd740b1dc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a large-scale operation across Beit Anan, Beit Duqqu, Biddu, Qatanna, Al-Qubeiba, Beit Surik, and Beit Iksa northwest of East Jerusalem, detaining or arresting around 50 Palestinians, raiding homes and imposing closures.
* In Anata, Israeli forces and settlers attacked Palestinians harvesting olives, injuring several and arresting a number of people, while settlers uprooted around 100 productive olive trees.
* Settlers also cut down around 50 olive trees in Mikhmas, while Israeli Nature Authority crews uprooted trees on Palestinian land in Wadi Al-Rababa in Silwan.
* **More than 20,500 students killed in Gaza over three years of Israeli genocide:** More than 20,500 school and university students were [killed](https://substack.com/redirect/adf7a131-3523-4d27-a32c-4bdefce9ddfa?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in Gaza during three years of Israel's war on the Strip since October 7, 2023, according to the Palestinian Ministry of Education.
* The ministry said more than 19,189 school students and 1,386 university students were killed, while 28,586 school students and 3,082 university students were injured.
* Israeli attacks also killed 805 school staff and 246 university lecturers and staff, and completely destroyed more than 179 government schools, more than 105 UNRWA schools and over 63 university buildings in Gaza.
* **Palestinian female prisoner held in isolation for 46 days:** Israeli prison authorities transferred 33-year-old Palestinian administrative detainee Bushra Al-Tawil to the isolation wing at Ohalei Oz Prison in Beersheba after 46 consecutive days in isolation, Palestinian prisoners' organizations said Wednesday.
* Al-Tawil, who has been detained without charge or trial since February, was initially isolated at Damon Prison before being transferred to Neve Tirza and then Ohalei Oz.
* The groups said lawyers have repeatedly sought permission to visit her but have been denied access. Under the UN Nelson Mandela Rules, solitary confinement lasting more than 15 consecutive days is prohibited.
* **Hamas marks third anniversary of October 7:** Hamas marked the third anniversary of the October 7, 2023 attack on Israel, describing it as a "historic and honorable milestone in our ongoing struggle" and saying it brought the Palestinian cause back to global attention after "decades of neglect, acquiescence and complicity" with Israeli policies.
* The group described October 7 as a "natural response" to decades of Israeli occupation, siege, killings and denial of Palestinian rights, as well as efforts to assert Israeli control over Al-Aqsa Mosque. "The conflict with the enemy did not begin on that day, nor have its final chapters yet been written," Hamas said.

* **More than 201,000 displaced by fighting in Yemen:** More than 201,000 people were [forced](https://substack.com/redirect/e43c69a0-1c0d-4458-879d-5389f0af3427?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) from their homes by the latest fighting in Yemen, with nearly all displaced since September 1, the International Organization for Migration (IOM) said Wednesday.

* **Puigdemont to return to Spain after court ruling** : Following a ruling from Spain's Constitutional Court that an amnesty law for Catalan separatists [covers](https://substack.com/redirect/d2d1e3e4-10a9-4a27-9311-84745fd621c9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the embezzlement charges against self-exiled Catalan leader Carles Puigdemont, a Supreme Court judge lifted an arrest warrant against him on Tuesday, clearing the way for his return without fear of arrest.
* Puigdemont fled to Belgium in 2017 after the Catalan independence referendum, which Madrid called illegal, and has since avoided several extradition attempts.
* **Australia 's High Court blocks Mount Pleasant coal mine expansion over emissions: **Three of five judges in Australia's High Court [ruled](https://substack.com/redirect/22ba2980-46b9-4d92-965e-a3fddd622331?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Wednesday that the expansion of the Mount Pleasant mine in New South Wales's Hunter Valley must be halted, noting that planning authorities had failed to find that greenhouse gas emissions from the facility were "minimised to the greatest extent practicable."
* Retired science teachers Wendy Wales and Tony Lonergan, who had fought for years against the facility's expansion, brought the case before the court. Operator Mach Energy, owned by a subsidiary of Indonesia's Salim Group, had sought to extend the open-cut mine's life by more than 20 years, to 2048, and nearly double its annual output.
* Australian environmental activists called it the court's first ruling on climate change and said it sets a "binding national precedent" requiring climate damage to be weighed when fossil fuel projects are considered.
* **U.S. troops in Okinawa get month-long curfew, alcohol ban after Marine accused of murdering local woman:** U.S. soldiers [stationed](https://substack.com/redirect/d4035aa0-ef14-4410-b261-91ccb31df2f6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in Okinawa have been given a month-long curfew and are banned from drinking alcohol while they undergo discipline training, according to a statement issued to service members on Tuesday, which also announced that U.S. military would pause its operations on the island for 48 hours to train soldiers on "standards and discipline."
* The ban follows the Tuesday arrest of Lance Cpl. Devin Jacob Ballard, 20, was accused of murdering and robbing 39-year-old Anna Yagi in a Naha hotel on Saturday. Japanese Police told Stars and Stripes that Yagi died of asphyxiation after Ballard allegedly "pressed on her neck," and that he took her wallet and backpack. Ballard denies the allegations.
* **Pacific climate ministers say world is "hurtling past" 1.5°C limit at pre-COP31 talks in Fiji**: On Tuesday, about 30 nations meeting in Fiji after a visit to Tuvalu [adopted](https://substack.com/redirect/b09697da-5497-4f14-a360-0d49f28529ac?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the Taku Pakasoa declaration calling for "deep, rapid and sustained emissions reductions."
* Fijian climate minister Lynda Tabuya told representatives from more than 30 countries at a separate conference in Nadi on Wednesday that "we are hurtling past the 1.5-degree temperature limit," adding that "overshoot is not a verdict we accept quietly" and that keeping 1.5 alive is "the primary legal obligation and duty we are here to uphold."
* Pacific nations are trying to lock in priorities ahead of COP31 in Antalya, Turkey, in November, including better access to climate finance, ocean protection and honoring the 1.5°C goal, despite UN projections that it will soon be exceeded. UN Environment Programme regional director Dechen Tsering said exceeding 1.5°C is now unavoidable and that each additional 100 years above it would commit the world to about 40 cm of extra median sea level rise by 2300.

Christa Pike conscious and speaking after surviving botched Tennessee execution, lawyers say. Archdiocese of St. Louis sues ICE, Missouri county officials over blocked sacraments for detainees. 18-year Interior Department lawyer resigns, citing "assault on the rule of law. Six progressive House members take on Israeli campaign against Palestinian health workers. International: Kenya confirms first Ebola case after death of traveler from DR Congo. Sudanese army chief Abdel Fattah al-Burhan vows to seize "every inch" of territory held by paramilitary Rapid Support Forces, rejecting negotiations. RSF attack kills 10 in West Kordofan. Another 105 Nigerians repatriated from South Africa, bringing total to 1,926 since June. Bulgarian Prime Minister Rumen Radev says drones hit two commercial ships in Black Sea, sinking one.
