This is Drop Site Daily, our free news recap We send it Monday - Friday Palestine Killed and wounded in Gaza: Over the past 24 hours, five Palestinians were killed--four in new Israeli attacks and one due to wounds sustained in an earlier attack--and 11 injured across Gaza, according to the Palestinian Ministry of Health. The total recorded death toll since October 7, 2023 is now 74,250 killed, with 175,278 injured. Since October 11, 2025, the first full day of the so-called ceasefire, Israel has killed at least 1,467 Palestinians in Gaza and wounded 5,161, while 836 bodies have been recovered. Israel continues to kill Palestinians in Gaza three years into the genocide: Four Palestinians were by Israeli fire and strikes across the Gaza Strip since dawn on Wednesday, according to WAFA. A Palestinian Civil Defence member was shot and killed by Israeli forces during an attempt to evacuate people wounded in Jabalia. A young boy was shot and killed amid heavy Israeli fire east of Khan Younis. Another Palestinian was killed in an Israeli drone strike in Khan Younis, while a fourth was killed in an Israeli airstrike on a refugee camp in the city. Palestinian killed, dozens detained as Israeli forces and settlers attack across the occupied West Bank: Nablus: A 44-year-old Palestinian was killed and nine others wounded, one seriously, after Israeli settlers accompanied by Israeli forces olive harvesters from Burqa in the Ramin plain between Nablus and Tulkarm on Wednesday, according to WAFA. Seven other Palestinians were injured after being beaten by Israeli forces in Nablus. Israeli forces also imposed a curfew on Nablus city, raided homes and detained several Palestinians, including journalist Umair Staitiyeh, while turning Karman School into a field interrogation center. In Al-Lubban Al-Sharqiya, settlers accompanied by Israeli forces erected dozens of Israeli flags between Palestinian homes and businesses. Ramallah: Israeli forces a curfew on Burqa, east of Ramallah as settlers raided the village. In Al-Mughayyir, settlers attacked Palestinian homes and set fire to a vehicle belonging to foreign journalists who were in the village documenting Israeli and settler attacks. Bethlehem: Settlers accompanied by Israeli forces entered Palestinian farmland in Al-Minya, southeast of Bethlehem, and harvested olives. Landowners have reportedly been prevented from reaching their land for more than a month. Jenin: A Palestinian man was by Israeli forces during a raid in central Jenin. Israeli forces also closed several gates and roads across the governorate, raided homes, demolished a memorial in Ya'bad, and removed photographs of Palestinians killed by Israel. East Jerusalem: Israeli forces a large-scale operation across Beit Anan, Beit Duqqu, Biddu, Qatanna, Al-Qubeiba, Beit Surik, and Beit Iksa northwest of East Jerusalem, detaining or arresting around 50 Palestinians, raiding homes and imposing closures. In Anata, Israeli forces and settlers attacked Palestinians harvesting olives, injuring several and arresting a number of people, while settlers uprooted around 100 productive olive trees. Settlers also cut down around 50 olive trees in Mikhmas, while Israeli Nature Authority crews uprooted trees on Palestinian land in Wadi Al-Rababa in Silwan. More than 20,500 students killed in Gaza over three years of Israeli genocide: More than 20,500 school and university students were in Gaza during three years of Israel's war on the Strip since October 7, 2023, according to the Palestinian Ministry of Education. The ministry said more than 19,189 school students and 1,386 university students were killed, while 28,586 school students and 3,082 university students were injured. Israeli attacks also killed 805 school staff and 246 university lecturers and staff, and completely destroyed more than 179 government schools, more than 105 UNRWA schools and over 63 university buildings in Gaza. Palestinian female prisoner held in isolation for 46 days: Israeli prison authorities transferred 33-year-old Palestinian administrative detainee Bushra Al-Tawil to the isolation wing at Ohalei Oz Prison in Beersheba after 46 consecutive days in isolation, Palestinian prisoners' organizations said Wednesday. Al-Tawil, who has been detained without charge or trial since February, was initially isolated at Damon Prison before being transferred to Neve Tirza and then Ohalei Oz. The groups said lawyers have repeatedly sought permission to visit her but have been denied access. Under the UN Nelson Mandela Rules, solitary confinement lasting more than 15 consecutive days is prohibited. Hamas marks third anniversary of October 7: Hamas marked the third anniversary of the October 7, 2023 attack on Israel, describing it as a "historic and honorable milestone in our ongoing struggle" and saying it brought the Palestinian cause back to global attention after "decades of neglect, acquiescence and complicity" with Israeli policies. The group described October 7 as a "natural response" to decades of Israeli occupation, siege, killings and denial of Palestinian rights, as well as efforts to assert Israeli control over Al-Aqsa Mosque. "The conflict with the enemy did not begin on that day, nor have its final chapters yet been written," Hamas said. Hamas said it and other Palestinian factions remain committed to their obligations under the Gaza ceasefire agreement and called on the U.S. and mediators to compel Israel to implement its commitments, including "a comprehensive and complete end to all forms of aggression," humanitarian relief, reconstruction and "the full withdrawal" of Israeli forces from Gaza. Leading ultra-Orthodox rabbi makes comments critical of Zionism, sparking backlash: Rabbi Dov Lando, the 96-year-old head of the Slabodka Yeshiva and a leading authority in Israel's Lithuanian Haredi community, said in footage aired Monday by Israel's Channel 12 that Jews "could live well with the Arabs without a state" and that "it would have been quite good if the Arabs ruled here." The footage was recorded about a year and a half ago at his home in Bnei Brak. He also said Zionism "made the Arabs hate us" and brought "physical disasters, not only spiritual ones" on Jews. He is an important religious authority for Degel HaTorah, part of the United Torah Judaism alliance that has been central to Netanyahu's governments. Former Prime Minister Naftali Bennett called Lando's comments "shame and disgrace" and attempted to link them to his political rival, Netanyahu. Former military chief Gadi Eisenkot and Member of the Knesset Avigdor Liberman also condemned Lando's comments. EU "ready to deploy" observers for Palestinian legislative elections in November: EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas Tuesday the bloc is "ready to deploy" election observers for the Palestinian legislative elections Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas has set for November 28. Kallas, who spoke with Palestinian Vice President Hussein Al-Sheikh on Tuesday, said Palestinians have the right to "credible, inclusive and transparent" elections and that, after nearly 20 years without a parliamentary vote, the polls would offer "a long-overdue opportunity to renew the legitimacy of Palestinian institutions." Hamas won the last Palestinian parliamentary elections, held in January 2006, securing a massive and unexpected majority and defeating the long-ruling Fatah movement. At the time, Hamas leader Ismail Haniyeh attempted to reassure the international community that the group was a "mature movement" that was politically open. Yet the victory was followed almost immediately by severe Israeli economic and military measures against the Hamas-led government. Yemen Missiles strike near Aden airport; Ansarallah says it targeted Saudi military supplies: Two ballistic missiles and several explosive-laden drones targeted the area around Aden International Airport early Wednesday, according to Yemen's Saudi-backed government. Ansarallah later it launched ballistic missiles claiming to have been targeting Saudi military supplies that had arrived at Badr Camp, adjacent to the airport. Ansarallah's military spokesperson claimed the attack killed and wounded a number of Saudi officers at Badr Camp and warned against using the civilian airport for "any military purposes." Yemen's Transport Ministry said one missile landed near the runway just "minutes" before Yemenia flight 603 from Cairo was due to land, forcing the aircraft to divert to Jeddah. Passengers and airport staff were evacuated, while two aircraft on the ground were moved after drones were detected over Aden. The airport later resumed flights. Ansarallah targets Saudi capital with ballistic missile: The Saudi-led coalition fighting in Yemen Wednesday that it intercepted and destroyed a ballistic missile north of the Saudi capital, Riyadh, which it said was launched by Ansarallah. Ansarallah later said its forces had targeted King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh with a ballistic missile, claiming it struck its target and disrupted air traffic. A coalition spokesperson said intelligence systems were tracking the missile's launch platform over the Yemeni capital, Sana'a, and that the coalition intended to target and destroy it. Saudi-backed Yemeni forces claim gains in Taiz highlands; Ansarallah repels advance in Al-Jawf: Forces aligned with Yemen's Saudi-backed government said they had tightened control over the highest peak in Jabal Habashi district and launched an offensive to retake the mountainous Al-Wazi'iyah district from Ansarallah. The fighting is part of a broader battle for the high ground east of Mocha and Bab al-Mandab, where control of mountain positions provides a strategic advantage over routes toward the Red Sea coast. Ansarallah officials, meanwhile, maintain that the group remains in control of Mocha and Bab al-Mandab. Separately, Ansarallah's military spokesperson said its forces repelled Saudi-backed forces attempting to advance on positions in eastern Al-Jawf governorate, claiming they targeted troop concentrations with ballistic missiles and drones. Ansarallah also claimed it shot down a Saudi CH-4 armed reconnaissance drone over Al-Jawf. More than 201,000 displaced by fighting in Yemen: More than 201,000 people were from their homes by the latest fighting in Yemen, with nearly all displaced since September 1, the International Organization for Migration (IOM) said Wednesday. The number has surged from 76,000 in mid-September to 201,217 people, or 33,776 households, and now spans 10 governorates. Taiz is the hardest hit, accounting for 57% of the total displaced. More than 3,700 people have also fled Yemen by sea to Djibouti, most of them women and children. "People are running for their lives and finding nowhere safe to go," IOM Director General said, warning that Yemen's humanitarian response plan is only 20% funded. Iran Iran says U.S. attacks damaged 111 petrochemical and pharmaceutical facilities: U.S. military attacks on Iran had 111 petrochemical and pharmaceutical facilities, disrupting supply chains and affecting Tehran's implementation of the Chemical Weapons Convention, Iran's representative to the Organization for the Prohibition of Chemical Weapons (OPCW) said Tuesday. Farajvand told the OPCW Executive Council in The Hague that the attacks damaged 60 petrochemical complexes, 44 pharmaceutical factories and seven other pharmaceutical facilities. Vance demands Iran curb uranium enrichment to end war: U.S. Vice President JD Vance Iran must make a "meaningful" reduction in its uranium enrichment capacity to secure an agreement with Washington. "If you don't want a nuclear weapon, then why do you need 60% enriched fuel?" Vance told Reuters, calling enrichment a "basic threshold issue." He said Washington remained open to an agreement but would demand concrete steps: "We're not going to trade words for actions." Iran has reiterated that the nuclear file is not part of its current discussions with Washington and that it is not considering opening such negotiations while the war continues. Vance claimed the U.S. was in contact with Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian and Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi, but added that "it's not totally clear how their country makes decisions." Rubio claims Iran has lost "complete control" of Strait of Hormuz: U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio claimed Wednesday that Iran has "lost complete control" of the Strait of Hormuz and said oil flows through the critical waterway had returned to pre-closure levels, despite continued attacks on commercial vessels. "The Strait of Hormuz is open and the quantities of oil exiting through it now are exactly the same as the quantities that were exiting before its closure," Rubio said at a news conference in Athens. His comments came as IRGC adviser Mohammad Reza Naqdi said Iran would soon completely block transit routes in the Strait it considers illegal, including passages he said had been created by blasting through rocky areas and were being used by small boats smuggling oil. Rubio also said the U.S. has the military "ability to provide security" in the Middle East, while accusing Iran of seeking to drive U.S. forces from the region and build a conventional military capability "so massive that they would become untouchable." Three Iranian men on trial in London accused of spying on Iran International journalists for Tehran: Prosecutors a London jury Tuesday that three Iranian citizens surveilled British-based journalists at Iran International, a Persian-language station opposed to the Iranian government and based in London, on behalf of Iran's foreign intelligence service between August 2024 and March 2025. Prosecutor Bill Emlyn Jones claimed these men were part of an effort to subject one or more of these journalists to "serious violence, no doubt as retribution for their criticism of the Iranian regime," with one of the men allegedly planning to carry out the attack. The three allegedly researched at least two journalists, visited addresses linked to them and took photos and videos. Each denies the charges against them. Emlyn also said that two of the men told police they did not know they were helping Iranian intelligence, while one said he did know the purpose of the activities but clarified that he was "bullied or threatened into doing what he did." Lebanon Israeli drone pursues residents in southern Lebanon as ceasefire violations continue: An Israeli drone Lebanese residents to their homes in the town of Yater in the Bint Jbeil district of southern Lebanon, Lebanon's National News Agency reported. Israeli artillery also shelled Wadi Zibqin in the Tyre (Sour) district. Hezbollah marks third anniversary of October 7: Hezbollah said Wednesday that three years of Israel's war on Gaza had failed to eliminate Hamas and other Palestinian factions or produce lasting security, in a statement marking the third anniversary of the Hamas-led October 7, 2023 attack. Hezbollah opened a support front against Israel from southern Lebanon on October 8, 2023, a day after the attack. Hezbollah described the October 7 attack as a "justified and legitimate act of resistance," arguing that it returned Palestine to the center of international attention and disrupted what it called the region's "defeatist normalization trajectory." The group reiterated its support for Palestinian factions, while issuing a warning to governments across the region. "Silence, accommodation and appeasement of the enemy and its allies will only lead to the undermining of their rule, their weakening, and enabling the enemy to determine the future of their countries and peoples," Hezbollah said. U.S. News U.S. trade deficit tops $100 billion in August, first time since March 2025: The U.S. trade deficit $12.7 billion from July to $105.6 billion in August, a 17-month high, according to Census Bureau and Bureau of Economic Analysis data released Tuesday. Imports grew 2.9 percentage points faster than exports. Crude oil exports rose $2 billion, and imports of crude oil, nonmonetary gold, and semiconductors rose $3.3 billion, $3.1 billion, and $2.4 billion, respectively. Trump says he is weighing suspension of federal gas tax : President Donald Trump Tuesday that his administration is "thinking about" suspending the federal gasoline tax. Any suspension would require an act of Congress, since the president cannot unilaterally suspend the tax. The national average for regular gas was $4.3685 a gallon Tuesday, according to AAA, more than a dollar above a year ago. The federal tax is 18.4 cents a gallon on gasoline and 24.4 cents on diesel. Dropping it would cut about 4 percent from the price of a gallon of regular and cost the highway and public transit fund more than $23 billion a year. Cook shifts three Senate races toward Democrats: Cook Political Report three Senate races leftward Tuesday: Kansas from "Lean Republican" to "Toss Up," New Hampshire from "Toss Up" to "Lean Democrat," and North Carolina from "Lean Democrat" to "Likely Democrat." The change raises Democrats' possible pickups from two to six seats; they need a net gain of four for a majority in the chamber. Paramount closes Warner Bros. Discovery deal: Paramount its acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery on Tuesday, giving David Ellison control of a combined company now called Skydance that owns Warner Bros. and Paramount Pictures, CNN and CBS News, and HBO Max and Paramount+. Following the merger, the ratings agency Fitch downgraded the combined company, which owes a total of $82 billion to its creditors, citing higher debt and "significant execution and integration risks." Ellison made nine offers to win the company over rival bidder Netflix and drew criticism for courting President Trump during the Justice Department review, including by hosting an April dinner "honoring the Trump White House." A coalition of state attorneys general sued to block the deal on antitrust grounds but settled for concessions, including an editorial independence board for CNN and an extra $1.5 billion for movies over five years. Whistleblower says Trump demanded FBI probe of anti-ICE protesters over a TikTok video: Jill Fields , a former supervisory intelligence analyst in the FBI's Los Angeles field office, in a whistleblower complaint to the Senate Judiciary Committee that the bureau opened preliminary investigations into anti-ICE protesters in Southern California in early 2025 after demands from President Trump and other officials, in violation of law and FBI policy. In one case, after a February 2025 protest in Alhambra, her squad was ordered to run pre-assessment checks on two to four protesters seen in a TikTok video using bullhorns to warn neighbors about immigration agents, though FBI policy bars investigations based solely on First Amendment activity and there was no evidence of a crime. Her lawyers' letter says FBI Director Kash Patel told senior leaders Trump "was angry about the incident, and he wanted those protesters investigated and arrested." The complaint describes a second incident weeks earlier in which then-Acting Deputy Attorney General Emil Bove demanded an investigation of protesters outside a federal building in California. When Fields raised concerns, a superior told her it had to happen. She says she was later stripped of her team, lost leadership support, and resigned. Sen. Chris Murphy denied entry to Al Udeid Air Base in Qatar : Sen.Chris Murphy (D-Conn.) reporters Tuesday he was barred from entering Al Udeid Air Base, the largest U.S. Air Force installation in the Middle East, during a congressional trip to the region, and that the Pentagon also refused to arrange a briefing on the Iran war. Murphy said that he wanted to see "the damage [the war has] caused to our facilities in the region and how it's harmed our relationships with partners," adding that his refusal was a part of "an active, unprecedented, unconstitutional effort underway to hide the costs" of the Iran war from Congress. A senior Defense Department official told The Washington Sun that Murphy's office was informed before the trip that he would not get access, citing War Secretary Pete Hegseth 's March directive on travel restrictions in the area, which the official said the department "applies... evenly." Christa Pike conscious and speaking after surviving botched Tennessee execution, lawyers say : Christa Pike , 50, who two doses of pentobarbital during the Sept. 30 execution attempt, is conscious and speaking, her lawyers said Tuesday. She remains in critical care at a Nashville hospital, they added, noting that they expect a long recovery for Pike. Her lawyers, who have pressed the courts to investigate the injection, said she sustained burns and other injuries to her arm and remains handcuffed and shackled to her bed. On Tuesday, they also renewed their plea for Gov. Bill Lee to commute her sentence to life in prison. Sen. Marsha Blackburn , the front-runner in next month's governor's race, has suggested using the electric chair on Pike following her failed execution. Archdiocese of St. Louis sues ICE, Missouri county officials over blocked sacraments for detainees : The Archdiocese of St. Louis a federal lawsuit Monday against Ste. Genevieve County officials and ICE leadership, alleging First Amendment violations over restrictions that keep Catholic priests from delivering communion, hearing confessions, and celebrating Mass for immigrant detainees at the Ste. Genevieve County Jail. The suit says priests need private, face-to-face contact for those sacraments, but jail policy allows only visits through glass barriers using a phone system. Visits are limited to a single four-hour window on Sundays, in 30-minute first-come, first-served blocks. Following the diocese's requests for face-to-face visits, the jail's administrator allegedly told the diocese that "the visitation policy was implemented by ICE" and that he could not change it. 18-year Interior Department lawyer resigns, citing "assault on the rule of law": John Murdock , an attorney and self-described conservative Christian who Interior's legal office in 2002, stepped down Sept. 30, according to a resignation letter obtained by The Guardian. The letter cites "glaring legal flaws" and flouting of environmental rules under the Trump administration. Murdock cited an appearance by Matt Giacona , the director of the Bureau of Ocean Energy Management, at a December conference, where he claimed the administration was "upholding the highest environmental standards" in relation to a sale of oil and gas leases in the Gulf called BBG1. That sale has been under intense legal scrutiny, with environmental groups claiming that the administration bypassed several environmental laws to see it through. In his letter, Murdock, who worked on the Deepwater Horizon cleanup effort, also noted his disagreement with the administration's exemptions for Gulf oil and gas operations from the Endangered Species Act, with its recent shuttering of offshore wind projects, and with the payment of hundreds of millions of dollars to TotalEnergies to renounce its wind leases. Six progressive House members take on Israeli campaign against Palestinian health workers: Reps. Rashida Tlaib (Mich.), Ilhan Omar (Minn.), Jesus "Chuy" Garcia (Ill.), Summer Lee (Penn.), Pramila Jayapal(Wash.), and Delia Ramirez (Ill.) a statement Tuesday condemning Israel's attacks on Palestinian health workers. The letter notes that Israeli forces have killed "at least 1,700 Palestinian doctors, nurses, paramedics and other healthcare workers," destroyed dozens of hospitals, and arbitrarily detained hundreds of health workers, including at least 16 physicians still held in "inhumane conditions." The statement called this an "intentional policy designed to further occupation, apartheid, and genocide against the Palestinian people." 📥 Have a tip on Capitol Hill? Email DC Correspondent Julian Andreone at Julian@dropsitenews.com Other International News Kenya confirms first Ebola case after death of traveler from DR Congo: Kenya its first Ebola case on Tuesday, after a Kenyan national who had lived in the DRC for seven years died in Nairobi, according to Kenyan Health Secretary Aden Duale. The patient had been ill for about a month before traveling by road from the DRC to Kampala, Uganda, and flying to Nairobi on Saturday. Kenyan President William Ruto said at least eight family members and 21 healthcare workers have been quarantined and ordered an enhanced response. Duale also noted that his ministry had identified 28 contacts with the patient, and that it was tracing 23 passengers and four crew from the patient's Uganda flight. The DRC outbreak, its 17th, was declared May 15 and has killed more than 4,000 people, with confirmed cases reaching 8,300 across seven provinces. The WHO has warned the epidemic is "far from over" and on track to surpass the 2014-2016 West Africa outbreak, which killed more than 11,000 people. Sudan 's Burhan vows to seize "every inch" of RSF territory, rejecting negotiations: Sudanese army chief Abdel Fattah al-Burhan Tuesday at a gathering in Village 5, in the northern locality of Merowe, that the "military option" will continue until the Rapid Support Forces are removed from Sudan, according to the Sudan News Agency. RSF attack kills 10 in West Kordofan: An RSF attack 10 civilians in Abu Ajal village, in the southeastern countryside of En Nahud in West Kordofan, according to the Dar Hamar Emergency Committee. RSF forces have reportedly been massing in the state following advances by the Sudanese army toward En Nahud and Al Khuway and its recent gains in North Kordofan. Ukraine launches 650-drone attack toward Moscow, killing two and igniting warehouse fire, Russian officials say: Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin on Tuesday that Ukrainian forces launched an overnight assault involving 650 drones heading toward the city, most of which he claimed were shot down. Two people were killed in nearby Radumlya and Barbybino, and seven were injured, according to a regional governor, who said the attacks also damaged 47 houses, four apartments and three cars. Russian war blogger Yuri Podolyaka said an oil storage tank was hit at the Volodarskaya facility, the biggest fuel depot in the Moscow region, which stores diesel, petrol and jet fuel and supplies all three of the capital's large airports; there was no official confirmation. Mali 's army retakes Kidal five months after separatists seized it: Mali's armed forces entered the northern city of Kidal on Tuesday, and the transitional government said troops had "consolidated their positions" after "intense air-ground neutralization operations" supported by "their Russian partners," according to a statement aired on state television. The Tuareg separatist Azawad Liberation Front (FLA) said it carried out a "strategic and controlled withdrawal" from the city to "preserve human lives," noting in its statement the "disproportionate use of aerial assets by Russian mercenaries from Africa Corps." It called its exit "temporary," and said the army entered Kidal without a fight. Another 105 Nigerians repatriated from South Africa, bringing total to 1,926 since June: A spokesperson for Nigeria's foreign ministry on Tuesday that another 105 Nigerians arrived in Lagos from South Africa on Friday, bringing the number of Nigerians repatriated from South Africa since June to 1,926. The latest group included 26 men, 29 women, and 50 children and was the 14th consular evacuation flight since the program began on June 10, following a wave of attacks on immigrants in South Africa. Indian police briefly detain opposition lawmakers, including Rahul Gandhi, at march demanding election chief 's resignation: Police in New Delhi briefly several opposition legislators on Tuesday, including Congress leader Rahul Gandhi, for trying to breach barricades during a march to demand the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, AFP reported. Gandhi was released shortly after being arrested. The roughly 1 km march ran from parliament to the Election Commission headquarters. Protesters, urged to action by the Gen-Z-led "Cockroach Janta Party," accuse the commission of manipulating voter registrations to benefit Prime Minister Narendra Modi's BJP. Bulgaria 's Radev says drones hit two commercial ships in Black Sea, sinking one: Bulgarian Prime Minister Rumen Radev sea and aerial drones struck two commercial vessels at about 3 a.m. Tuesday, roughly 70 nautical miles off Bulgaria's coast, calling it an "unacceptable attack in Bulgaria's exclusive economic zone" and "a blatant violation of international law and maritime law." He did not identify the source of the drone attacks. The Togo-flagged Alfa Watan suffered critical structural damage and sank, and Bulgarian authorities launched a major search for its missing crew, the Prime Minister said. The Palau-flagged Able, reportedly carrying wheat, also caught fire, with a Bulgarian ferry and naval boat evacuating all 18 crew. France suspends high school classes for the rest of the week as student protests spread: Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu high school classes nationwide through the end of the week after protests demanding education reforms on Tuesday drew anywhere from a quarter to a half a million people. Lecornu framed this week's suspension as a way to let schools pursue "internal democracy" and ordered ministers to address the students' demands, which include replacing absent teachers and changing the school day, by the end of October. Unions for farmers, energy workers and teachers have joined the demonstrations. Police fired tear gas in several cities, and protests turned violent at times in Strasbourg, Lyon and Rennes, with protesters lighting fires and throwing projectiles. France's interior ministry says 6,100 people have been arrested, mostly under 18, and the justice ministry says more than 1,800 will be prosecuted, including 1,483 minors. Puigdemont to return to Spain after court ruling : Following a ruling from Spain's Constitutional Court that an amnesty law for Catalan separatists the embezzlement charges against self-exiled Catalan leader Carles Puigdemont, a Supreme Court judge lifted an arrest warrant against him on Tuesday, clearing the way for his return without fear of arrest. Puigdemont fled to Belgium in 2017 after the Catalan independence referendum, which Madrid called illegal, and has since avoided several extradition attempts. Australia 's High Court blocks Mount Pleasant coal mine expansion over emissions: Three of five judges in Australia's High Court Wednesday that the expansion of the Mount Pleasant mine in New South Wales's Hunter Valley must be halted, noting that planning authorities had failed to find that greenhouse gas emissions from the facility were "minimised to the greatest extent practicable." Retired science teachers Wendy Wales and Tony Lonergan, who had fought for years against the facility's expansion, brought the case before the court. Operator Mach Energy, owned by a subsidiary of Indonesia's Salim Group, had sought to extend the open-cut mine's life by more than 20 years, to 2048, and nearly double its annual output. Australian environmental activists called it the court's first ruling on climate change and said it sets a "binding national precedent" requiring climate damage to be weighed when fossil fuel projects are considered. U.S. troops in Okinawa get month-long curfew, alcohol ban after Marine accused of murdering local woman: U.S. soldiers in Okinawa have been given a month-long curfew and are banned from drinking alcohol while they undergo discipline training, according to a statement issued to service members on Tuesday, which also announced that U.S. military would pause its operations on the island for 48 hours to train soldiers on "standards and discipline." The ban follows the Tuesday arrest of Lance Cpl. Devin Jacob Ballard, 20, was accused of murdering and robbing 39-year-old Anna Yagi in a Naha hotel on Saturday. Japanese Police told Stars and Stripes that Yagi died of asphyxiation after Ballard allegedly "pressed on her neck," and that he took her wallet and backpack. Ballard denies the allegations. Pacific climate ministers say world is "hurtling past" 1.5°C limit at pre-COP31 talks in Fiji: On Tuesday, about 30 nations meeting in Fiji after a visit to Tuvalu the Taku Pakasoa declaration calling for "deep, rapid and sustained emissions reductions." Fijian climate minister Lynda Tabuya told representatives from more than 30 countries at a separate conference in Nadi on Wednesday that "we are hurtling past the 1.5-degree temperature limit," adding that "overshoot is not a verdict we accept quietly" and that keeping 1.5 alive is "the primary legal obligation and duty we are here to uphold." Pacific nations are trying to lock in priorities ahead of COP31 in Antalya, Turkey, in November, including better access to climate finance, ocean protection and honoring the 1.5°C goal, despite UN projections that it will soon be exceeded. body:
Three states are about to decide a lot more than 2026.

| | | |
---
Patriot,
---
We've looked at the polling in every swing state and swing race in the country. It's margin of error, either way, almost everywhere.

At this point, it's not about winning anybody over. _It's about who actually shows up._

If conservatives turn out in November, we'll win every critical battleground and lay the groundwork for victory in 2028 and beyond.

That's why Turning Point Action is focusing all our efforts on three key states: Arizona, Nevada, and New Hampshire.

**We call these states the new RED WALL.**

_Let me explain why they matter so much... _

After 2024, Charlie looked at the numbers, looked at the maps, and told our team something simple. If we lock down Arizona, Nevada, and New Hampshire, the Left's entire strategy falls apart. Their map collapses. Their path back to power disappears.

Here's why... Winning the presidency comes down to 270 electoral votes. Lose Arizona and most of the realistic paths to the White House in 2028 are gone. Lose Nevada and New Hampshire and the Left rebuilds the Blue Wall they lost in 2024.

Whoever wins in 2028 controls the 2030 Census. The Census drives redistricting. Redistricting sets the congressional map for the next ten years.

This midterm decides which way that goes.

body:

**Good Morning!
** **American traditions are disappearing --and some are fading faster than you might think.** Remember the traditions you grew up with and somehow just...stopped doing? Maybe you haven't thought about them since you were a kid. But across America, familiar rituals that were once simply part of life are quietly vanishing--and **the numbers behind their decline may surprise you.** Which Sunday tradition did families once build their entire week around? Meet Joe Males:

**Joe Males is a Marine Veteran, small business-owner, city council member, and most importantly, a father. Throughout his life, he has put service to his community at the forefront of his life’s mission.

Shortly after turning 18, Joe enlisted in the Marine Corps. He attended boot camp in Camp Pendleton and later served overseas in the Philippines and Guam. After being discharged as a Sergeant, Joe remained committed to supporting his fellow veterans. He took on leadership roles in his local Elks Lodge and American Legion post, working to ensure veterans in the community had the resources and support they deserved.

Following his time in the Marine Corps, Joe carried his strong work ethic and discipline into the field of computer networking services. He started in an entry-level position, worked his way through multiple leadership roles, and in 1996, he built his own business from the ground up. Joe knows firsthand the hard work and sacrifice of this journey, and he’s determined to make it easier for hardworking Americans to do the same.

Joe’s entry into politics was deeply personal. After his son, a Marine who followed in his footsteps, was tragically murdered back home, Joe vowed that no parent should have to endure such a loss. Determined to take a stand for public safety and the rule of law, he ran for Hemet City Council to help ensure no other family would experience the same tragedy.

During his tenure on the City Council, Joe has led numerous initiatives to improve infrastructure, drive business growth, and keep neighborhoods safe and clean. He takes pride in his ability to collaborate with fellow council members and get results, even when facing different perspectives. Joe is committed to bringing this same results-driven approach to Washington D.C., to ensure the voices of the American people are heard and their needs are met.

Hi, I’m sorry to bother you, but this is urgent — so I’ll keep it quick. Supreme Court Justice Samuel Alito just said that retirement is on the table for him next year. This news just tripled the stakes of our race. Susan Collins voted to confirm three of the Supreme Court justices who overturned Roe v. Wade, and she's voted with Donald Trump 96% of the time. If we lose Maine, we’ll lose the Senate. And if we lose the Senate, Susan Collins will almost certainly be the deciding vote for Trump’s fourth SCOTUS appointment. October 7th...
Nearly 2,500 dead.
I'm talking about American soldiers, Marines, sailors and airmen killed in Afghanistan, in a war that started 25 years ago today and bought us nothing.
They told us it was about "getting the men behind 9/11." But 15 of the 19 hijackers were Saudi. Or was George Bush in on it? And why did Building 7 implode for no reason? Good luck getting a straight answer on any of that. What we got was... _the Taliban._ Then it was girls' schools, nation-building and "democracy." Four presidents kept it going for 20 years.
Every one of those 2,500 came home in a flag-draped coffin. Roughly 20,000 more were wounded, and that number doesn't count the ones carrying something you can't see on an X-ray.
The ending was worse.
The Taliban was back in the presidential palace before our last plane left, 13 Americans died at Abbey Gate, and the autopen president left billions in American equipment for the people we'd spent two decades fighting.
Biden owns that exit. A disgrace. But the 20 years that made it inevitable belong to the whole Washington foreign policy club, Republican and Democrat alike.
Which brings me to the "other" October 7.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/31cd2fc2-22b9-4067-8ecd-60ac0e5ba1b5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Israel is a sovereign nation with one of the most capable militaries on earth, and it can fight its own wars._****_ Under the current agreement, American taxpayers send it $3.8 billion a year, promised through 2028.
When's the last time your town got a 10-year promise from Congress?
More than 30 states, including Idaho, have also passed laws punishing businesses or contractors who "boycott Israel."
[| | | | | Western Civ Maximalist
---
@brian_lenney
Idaho is taking federal debt to finance rural health care programs. One of the qualifications is you can't be against Israel to be a sub-recipient of the grant. Somebody should repeal this law next year .
| 8:06 PM * Jul 23, 2026 * 4.11K Views26 Replies * 19 Reposts * 128 Likes
---](https://substack.com/redirect/ac4185ca-eb12-4744-9c91-93b2dba5d72d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
In Texas, people have even been asked to sign a pledge about a foreign country to keep a state contract.
Then there's the money in our own elections. Pro-Israel PACs spent tens of millions in the 2024 primaries to knock out candidates they didn't like. If any other country's lobby did that, conservatives would be demanding answers, and I don't see why the standard should change.
George Washington warned about exactly this in his Farewell Address. A _" passionate attachment" _to another nation, he said, pulls you into its quarrels for no good reason. John Quincy Adams said America _" goes not abroad in search of monsters to destroy." _
_**That used to be the conservative position, and I 'd like it back.**_
If we're America First, then I want our border secured and our veterans taken care of before anyone else gets a check.
Here in Idaho, we've already started taking it back.
At our state convention in Meridian this June, the resolutions committee sent 19 resolutions to the floor. One of them affirmed support for Israel and condemned Hamas (resolutions like it passed at the last two conventions without much of a fight).
This time I moved to strike it, and the motion passed overwhelmingly:
[| | | | | Western Civ Maximalist
---
@brian_lenney
My (successful) motion today at the Idaho GOP Convention to remove the resolution regarding Israel: "This resolution is asking us to formally align Idaho's state party with a foreign nation's military objectives while our own Pentagon (June 5, 2026) says Israel is spying on us...
| 7:17 PM * Jun 20, 2026 * 7.79K Views52 Replies * 69 Reposts * 442 Likes
---](https://substack.com/redirect/23b60b13-83e0-41a3-b435-3cc91c7cbe85?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Nobody took a formal count, but the resolutions chair estimated about three-quarters of the delegates stood up for it.
Because the resolution asked Idhao Republicans to formally line up behind a foreign nation's military objectives, and to commend a U.S. president for foreign policy work on that country's behalf. It said nothing about wages or illegal immigration and it would have produced _exactly zero_ policy for Idaho.
Yet we were being asked to nod along with it just a few weeks after [NBC News reported](https://substack.com/redirect/01dd887c-5a7c-42c2-923b-c1beeac7a5e0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the Pentagon's Defense Intelligence Agency had raised its threat rating for Israeli spying on the U.S. to "critical," the highest level there is.
Delegates told the resolutions chair afterward they wanted resolutions about Idaho. That's what the vote said too.
And the same convention backed [a plank](https://substack.com/redirect/c68f5073-7f54-44cf-9952-7bd9326348d1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) saying the Idaho National Guard shouldn't be sent into combat overseas unless Congress actually declares war. Congress hasn't declared one since 1942. Afghanistan never got one either.
Like I said, Idaho still has its own [anti-boycott law](https://substack.com/redirect/83af5b7c-cd6f-4b6e-a360-93fa6c9b7c8c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on the books, passed in 2021. If America First is our position, that law belongs on the table next session.
Idaho isn't alone, either.
A [Pew survey in March](https://substack.com/redirect/23f98bca-24d5-4aa1-bd44-ea9990eab12c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) found 41% of Republicans now view Israel unfavorably, and among Republicans under 50 it's 57%, up from 50% a year earlier.
Since the convention, someone in my own party told me I should "stop talking about this." But I'm going to keep talking about it, because this is the Idaho GOP's position. Three-quarters of the room stood up for it.
Because no foreign nation should hold a permanent, untouchable place in American politics.****
**America First can 't come with an asterisk that says "except Israel."**

The numbers are in:**We 've successfully raised $25 million in our fight against Greg Abbott.** 13 million of those dollars were raised in the past three months, and a full $3 million were raised in the past two weeks alone.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/6b9fd8d6-d89a-42df-85d9-d660a906f91d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
But I promise, it's not really about the money. Since day one, this has been a people-powered campaign focused on ending Greg Abbott's corruption that puts billionaires first and Texans last. What I'm most impressed by is that hundreds of thousands of unique donors are chipping in and supporting my race. If that wasn't remarkable enough, 74% of the donors to my campaign this summer have never donated to us before. If the three polls that show me in the lead didn't convince you that we can win, hopefully that fact will.
**People are supporting this race because my plan is to secure the American Dream by saving our public schools and putting money in people 's pockets.** That's why people from _every_ corner of Texas and in every political party are investing in our campaign, volunteering, knocking on doors, and telling their neighbors if they want a better future for Texas, they need to vote for me. From now until Election Day, I will continue fighting for a Texas that puts working people first, because every Texan deserves the opportunity to achieve the American Dream.
$25 million raised is a huge milestone we've crossed, but I'll be honest, our race is far from over. We've raised a lot of money, but it doesn't match the mega-million dollar warchest we are competing with. Greg Abbott has spent over $124 million against me since the start of the cycle, and thanks to his megadonors, there's plenty more where that came from.
The momentum of our race has put a huge target on my back, and Abbott will only continue to launch more attack ads, spreading lies about me and my voting record. We can't let his lies go unanswered.
**[I wouldn't ask if it weren't important, but if you can, would you please consider chipping in $10, $5, or even $2 to my campaign to beat Greg Abbott? Every dollar truly does make a difference.](https://substack.com/redirect/6b9fd8d6-d89a-42df-85d9-d660a906f91d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
[DONATE NOW ->](https://substack.com/redirect/6b9fd8d6-d89a-42df-85d9-d660a906f91d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Let's keep going.
-- Gina

| | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | Peter,

Tickets are going fast for my **Inaugural Freedom Fish Fry** , and this is an event you don’t want to miss!
Join me **Friday, October 23, from 5:00 to 7:00 p.m. in Clarksville** for fish with all the fixings, fellowship, and an evening honoring those who have served our country.

**Tickets are $25 for adults, $15 for children, and FREE for veterans.**
**To our veterans:** This evening is about serving those who have served us. Your sacrifice has protected our freedom, and I would be honored to welcome you as my guest. Please reserve your free ticket at the link below.

I look forward to seeing you there!
**For Tennessee,**
**Matt Van Epps** Congressman, TN-07

Now let me tell you why this mission means so much to me. My name is Eduardo Verastegui. Several years ago, I learned firsthand about the horrific reality of child trafficking. What I heard broke my heart. Children were being bought and sold.
Families were being torn apart.
Lives were being destroyed. **I couldn't forget it.** **I couldn't stay silent.** I kept asking myself one question: **"What if it were my child?"** That question changed my life. What started as a film project became a mission and a calling. That calling eventually led me to help produce the film _Sound of Freedom_. **Not for fame.**
**Not for awards.**
**But because I believed people needed to see the truth.** For years, many people said the film would never succeed. Doors closed.
Studios walked away.
People told us to give up. **But when innocent children are suffering, silence is not an option.** And while the film helped awaken millions of people to this crisis, awareness alone is not enough. That is why we created the **Sound of Freedom Foundation**. Our mission is simple: **To stop the sale of God's children.**

A message that reminds the world that every child has God-given dignity. And importantly, a message that sparks conversations and helps raise awareness about a crisis many people still do not see. For years, many people said the film would never succeed. Doors closed. Studios walked away. People told us to give up. But when innocent children are suffering, silence is not an option. And while the film helped awaken millions of people to this crisis, awareness alone is not enough. That is why we created the Sound of Freedom Foundation. | | | | Peter, Yesterday, NPR broke the news that a tech startup called Valar Atomics has submitted an application to the Bureau of Land Management to seize more than 9,000 acres of federal public land near Price, Utah. They plan to build a sprawling AI data center complex dubbed "Project Beehive." To power it, they aren't just hooking up to the grid. They want to construct approximately 456 small nuclear reactors, build an on-site nuclear fuel fabrication facility, and permanently store radioactive nuclear waste right on our public land. The complex would consume 9.6 gigawatts of electricity—more than double the average power consumption of the entire state of Utah—all to keep corporate AI servers humming. And company documents reveal they want to break ground before the year is out. [**They want to turn 9,000 acres of your public lands into a private, nuclear-powered server city and radioactive waste dump. Will you chip in $10 today to help us stop projects like these in their tracks?**](https://go.sparkpostmail1.com/f/a/Lq-naowoRl7Ebbz_bTeEIw~~/AAUS1hA~/7W6D5JavOG94N4H9-cXJgtgLGtPwvcbeUswbSlArVQ09tzAf6pCRMgOMp-jxZ_37N7qe2fU359TqmbIdy_Vb2loOVh5iPeHm3uhgfyn61-0YO7mTOrnNPOGFeUDNGtqU9Luu-DQIauuiXp4Yhmt1buoECDjhbjWY0_SCHTr-wjoDXH849FGeIlkF80P48xdBGuL7pj1WnvpVXfT_QC5pguPZ6_mK8lG3l8-zCdmPbKxXkSeCqD6fYTzpcaEsbgzy) They want to do this on federal land because over 500 cities and counties across America have already restricted or outright banned data centers. Local communities don't want their water sucked dry, their electric rates spiked, and their neighborhoods industrialized. So Big Tech did what it always does: **it ran to Washington for a handout.** With less than a month until Election Day, we are going to make this toxic giveaway their worst political nightmare. At Public Land Warriors, we are dropping a surgical, inescapable digital ad blitz directly into the districts of the politicians rubber-stamping these backroom deals. We are going to ensure that every hunter, angler, camper, and voter knows exactly who is trying to turn our national heritage into a corporate nuclear park. Peter, **We recently polled 1,487 likely voters in Texas about Dan Patrick’s favorite campaign strategy:_AI Deepfakes._**

**According to our internal poll of Texans likely to vote (Democrats, Republicans, and Independents), 91% say the use of AI deepfakes in political campaigns is**** _unacceptable_****. ** **_That includes 84% of people who voted for Donald Trump in 2024._** You'd think that kind of overwhelming consensus would give Dan Patrick pause. _It hasn't._ Dan Patrick ran AI deepfake videos of me until we filed a police report. subject: We have some exciting events planned this weekend
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Voto Latino
body:
#
We have some exciting events planned this week, Peter.
Voto Latino and the Hispanic Federation are launching a major get out the vote operation targeting Texas’s Rio Grande Valley.
The Valley is ground zero for Latino political power, Peter. In 2024, 315,000 eligible Latino voters in the RGV sat out the election. On top of that, nearly 500,000 young Texas Latinos turned 18 in the last two years and are now eligible to cast their ballots for the first time.
**To put it plainly, the Rio Grande Valley is going to be the epicenter of the Latino vote for the rest of the country.** If the Latino vote in this area swings drastically back, it’s going to be the building block for what people can expect in 2028.
In order to turn this opportunity into real turnout on Election Day, we’re meeting voters directly on the ground.
**This Saturday, we are hosting a major community town hall in Edinburg, Texas, to help residents check their voter registration status, navigate voter roll purges, and make concrete early voting plans.** We’re following that with a televised town hall in partnership with Telemundo and a massive turnout rally right before Election Day.
[](https://act.votolatino.org/go/57?c0=em-ms-voto-20261007-1.bBXo6E&amount=3&refcode=em20261007-655&t=1&akid=655%2E1366028%2Ezs0JZ8)
Organizing town halls, running voter information drives, and putting field organizers on the ground across the Rio Grande Valley takes continuous resources.

Voto Latino

Yet here we are! 😅 It’s an honor, but the road getting to here was _far_ from glamorous. I had to leave my job to take the leap of faith and run for office. I drove for Uber at night to pay my bills. I was priced out of my apartment and had to couch-surf, even sleeping in my car on occasion until I found the next place. So how did I get here? How did I become the first Gen-Z member of Congress? **With the help of folks who refused to count me out:** My family, my friends, my community, civil rights leaders who came before me, and grassroots supporters like you - I can’t possibly list them all! **[_I’m going to keep using my voice in Congress to fight for change and to elect more progressive leaders in Florida and across the country, but I need your help to get the job done. Please, will you chip in $27 today to fuel our fight? >>_](http://clicksp.frostforcongress.com/f/a/hTvQ8FI3MM7CgGmaSUfncA~~/AAPPABA~/2rWYvj2LC_Z7AMMxY9qj59dQTXRU0JbYpjH5dNThRkDacr9xwkII7AbUXx4T-y0Rz_aODAKDYPqLgz626qug2lE488e-GYkI9ZG5E7scA8PeO5VBGWelB-9WMmH70k6-oVJuRBtllzAyaH73FcVNqNSs1keQ_Ac18tn9Aqv6oTBG7EGH4ctSuHlZ1H1PSgWJUbm9JdljljhXGIwLzUiHf6IfC5te6EDaRaPHJkeEQzez769AaoY7faMJliVa5CC64eBnM7nzOdZz0gJrwBFQHIIih3t9BsE6Vfs271Aw98kL4nPG8r6qHuEf0_WIsdB1obBJ03GvMSrmOciPI97DhJuKvy0dvxS15tK3SqOiwRk~)** Being the first (and only!) of a generation in an institutional body like Congress means a lot to me. Because not only am I representing my district, but I’m also representing an _entire_ generation. I didn’t run for Congress to be the first member of Gen Z elected, but it is a message for young people and everybody else out there: **Don’t count young people out!** Gen Z has seen and experienced a lot of awful things happen during our lives. U.S. Sen. Susan Collins (R) turned her first debate with Graham Platner's replacement into a test of the Democrat ex-Senate President Troy Jackson's record and command of government Tuesday, answering his attacks over President Donald Trump with questions about what Jackson accomplished in Augusta and how he would operate in Washington.
Jackson came ready to challenge Collins' vote for Supreme Court Justice Brett Kavanaugh, to which Collins reminded viewers that she'd also voted for Supreme Court Justices Elena Kagan, Sonia Sotomayor, and Ketanji Brown Jackson.
Collins attacked Jackson for lying on an application for a Federal Housing Administration (FHA) home loan to get a lower interest rate on a second home he eventually flipped for a roughly $80,000 profit. She also challenged his understanding of Medicaid and Medicare, in an exchange where Jackson appeared to confuse the two programs.
**[[RELATED: Maine Senate President Troy Jackson Locked in Bitter Legal Fight Over Augusta Home He Bought- and Moved Into - in 2019...]](https://substack.com/redirect/995afcb8-96f5-4881-b533-1e37a60bcb31?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**

[Upgrade to paid](https://substack..WvfWv5SXCNLp1t3ykfd2piJ8mF9_XVfgjELbJrMji7I?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget-preamble&utm_content=219285119)
Medicaid is a welfare program administered by the states -- a program Jackson voted to expand to able-bodied childless adults and non-citizens as Senate President. Medicare, on the other hand, is a federally administered program that provides health insurance to seniors.
The [hourlong CBS13/FOX23 debate](https://substack.com/redirect/1a22c897-db01-410d-8179-361629043da0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) is the first of four televised encounters before the Nov. 3 election. However, early voting has already begun in Maine, with enrolled Democrats disproportionately leading Republicans and unaffiliated voters in requests for absentee ballots.
For Collins, Chair of the powerful Senate Appropriations Committee, it was an opportunity to defend the value of her seniority. For Jackson, the former Maine Senate president who has emphasized his connections to labor unions, it was a chance to persuade voters that Collins would instead use another term to serve Elon Musk and President Donald Trump -- two names that Jackson repeated as if suffering from Tourette syndrome.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/63fbc60d-00a8-4615-9487-1b3b5f580798?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)| | |
#### [The Book of Troy: Five Tales from the Maine politics archives...](https://substack.com/redirect/63fbc60d-00a8-4615-9487-1b3b5f580798?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
---
| | [The Robinson Report](https://substack.com/profile/147548156-the-robinson-report)| | *
---|---|---
| Jul 22
| [| Read full story
---](https://substack.com/redirect/63fbc60d-00a8-4615-9487-1b3b5f580798?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Democrats are targeting Collins' seat as they try to win control of the Senate, with Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer (D-N.Y.) directing tens of millions of dollars in ad money and street activist funding to attack Collins and bolster Jackson.
Collins represents a state that Kamala Harris carried in 2024 -- while Trump carried the more conservative Second Congressional District for the third consecutive presidential election, making Maine a unique battleground in the national contest.
If successful, Schumer and his colleagues have made clear that they'd use control of the Senate to lead additional impeachment expeditions against Trump, as well as roll back his immigration policies.
Drawing a sharp contrast with Trump's immigration policies, Schumer even admitted this week that Democrats' goal is to [provide citizenship](https://substack.com/redirect/a4e7667a-e103-44ae-b2b3-d95338e326e0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) -- and eventually the right to vote -- to what he estimated as 11 million illegal aliens currently present in the U.S.
In last night's debate, Jackson indicated his opposition to the SAVE Act and state-level voter ID policies, saying that [voters](https://substack.com/redirect/3343bd44-cfe8-4daf-93b3-918dc3a18cfc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) should not have to show ID when casting a vote.
Jackson has had little time to build his Senate campaign.
After losing the Democratic primary for governor, he won the party's July 25 convention to replace Graham Platner, whom Jackson campaigned with as much as he could while seeking the Blaine House.
Platner withdrew from the Senate race amid multiple sexual assault allegations he denied. The switch left Jackson just over 100 days before the election, and he was installed as the nominee without any electoral input from Maine's unenrolled voters.
Collins began the debate with a list of federal investments. As Senate Appropriations Committee chair, she said, she had secured $1.5 billion for 672 Maine projects over five years, including housing, water systems, roads and rural hospitals.
"Effective leadership matters in Washington," she said in her [opening statement](https://substack.com/redirect/b5ef9719-9058-44cb-ab40-58972797ab23?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
Jackson used his opening to drop the first of many names he hoped to associate Collins with: Brett Kavanaugh.
"Senator Collins has had 30 years to show whose side she's on," he said.
The fight over affordability followed the same division. Collins blamed policies enacted in Augusta for high electricity rates, housing costs and property taxes. Jackson blamed Trump's tariffs, the Iran war and federal spending decisions, arguing that Collins had done too little to stop them.
"Those are all due to Augusta's failed policies under the failed leadership of Troy Jackson," Collins said of the costs she identified during the affordability exchange.
Jackson repeatedly attacked her role in advancing Trump's 2025 tax-and-spending legislation, which he blamed for cuts to assistance programs. But Jackson appeared to deliberately misrepresent how Collins voted on the so-called One Big Beautiful Bill Act -- a tactic that has also been adopted in many of the Schumer-funded ads airing throughout Maine.
"That's why that bill is crucifying Maine," he said.
Collins supported the [June 28, 2025, motion to begin considering the bill](https://substack.com/redirect/57989e5e-1b7b-47ad-b99d-4354ba10fa1f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), then opposed [final passage July 1](https://substack.com/redirect/dae8b7c6-b4d0-4b51-adbb-91b5d88f317b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). On Tuesday, she said advancing it allowed her to help secure a $50 billion rural health fund. Jackson argued that the fund could not make up for the legislation's harm.
Jackson ran into a more consequential problem when he blamed Collins' long tenure and appropriations chairmanship for inadequate Medicaid payments to Maine hospitals.
"Medicaid rates are set by the state," Collins said.
The [Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services](https://substack.com/redirect/6dc53354-7160-4873-bb3b-4fe9615a313a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) says states establish provider payment rates within federal requirements, with changes subject to federal review. Washington helps finance the program. The appropriations chair does not set Maine's hospital payment schedule.
Jackson also fumbled when he began attacking the role of private equity in buying up single-family housing in Maine, seemingly unaware that Collins had voted in favor of bipartisan legislation to prevent the practice. Rather than course-correct, Jackson doubled down, claiming that, if Collins really had supported such a law, then it wasn't working.
Collins then informed Jackson that the bill was in fact sponsored and co-authored by far-left Sen. Elizabeth Warren (D-Mass.) -- who initially endorsed Graham Platner as "my kind of man" before throwing her support behind Jackson.
Collins also used her opportunity to question Jackson directly to challenge his effectiveness as a legislator. She said more than a third of his bills had been unanimously rejected in committee and asked how he would succeed as the Senate's most junior member.
Jackson said the tally ignored duplicate bills and instances in which he let colleagues advance legislation and receive credit. He disputed Collins' account of the process and insisted she didn't understand how the State Legislature worked.
The debate fell on the eighth anniversary of Collins' confirmation vote, a date Jackson emphasized from his opening statement.
Collins defended judging nominees on their qualifications and pointed to her votes for justices nominated by Democratic presidents. She did not disavow the Kavanaugh confirmation.

"I clearly don't agree with how Brett Kavanaugh voted on Roe v. Wade," she said.
Asked directly by WGME moderator Gregg Laggerquist about pay-to-play allegations involving payments made to his lobbyist son, Jackson dodged the question.
Among the pay-to-play allegations facing Jackson is a $50,000 payment to his son Chace Jackson from the Maine Gun Safety Coalition. Less than one month after his son received that contract, Jackson flipped positions he'd held for 20 years on three key pieces of gun control legislation.
"Yeah. Well, I mean, my son, uh, didn't do anything wrong and independent fact checkers have proven that. Uh, time and time again that there was nothing there," he claimed.
Collins then pressed him about the FHA-insured mortgage on his Augusta house. He said he stayed there during the workweek and returned to Allagash on weekends.
In defending false statements he made to acquire the low-interest-rate loan, Jackson may have dug himself a different hole. During the debate, he said that he was working so hard in Augusta that he stayed there five days a week -- which stands in conflict with the mileage reimbursements he received as Senate President.
According to public records obtained under the Freedom of Access Act, Jackson received more reimbursement money during his time as Senate President than any lawmaker in the history of the state.
Collins closed by returning to the argument that has defined her campaign.
"To be effective in the Senate, you need knowledge, experience, seniority and relationships," she said.
Jackson challenged the premise that holding influence meant using it well. He said "power means nothing if you won't use it when the people in Maine need it."
In a deft parting shot as the credits began to roll, Collins -- who has kept true to her promise not to talk about the fact that Jackson fathered two children with his second cousin -- reminded viewers that the Democrat is a Steelers fan.

name: Elizabeth Warren
subject: Follow the money
disclaimer_text: paid for by the same people cashing in on his administration
body:
How Trump and his administration are benefiting from MAGA donors

| | | [ ](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/go/216?t=3&akid=3046%2E4032634%2ERcgEhU)
---
Want a government job? Need the regulators off your back? Hoping an investigation into your company quietly goes away? In Donald Trump's Washington, there's a way. Write a big check to MAGA Inc., the super PAC he calls: _**"My money that I control."**_ Researchers at the Center for American Progress Action Fund just followed the money, and MAGA Inc. has raised $404.6 million from donors writing checks of $100,000 or more. Of that $404.6 million, 79% came from just 108 donors who got a documented potential benefit from Trump or his administration Simply put: The people bankrolling Trump's super PAC are the same people profiting from his presidency. Here's what that looks like in reality:
* Twenty donors tied to government appointments, for themselves or their relatives and business partners, gave **$87.75 million.**
* Fifty-seven donors who benefited from regulatory rollbacks gave nearly **$82 million.**
* Seven donors who saw enforcement actions against them dropped or reversed gave **$78.6 million.**
* Six donors who've pulled in more than $11 billion in federal contracts, including private prison giant GEO Group, gave **$41.7 million.**
* Two donors connected to presidential pardons gave **$4.5 million.**

The single biggest industry writing checks? Crypto, at **$88.2 million.** Add it all up, and you get pay-to-play on a scale we've never seen. Trump promised to drain the swamp. Instead, he handed it a menu. And while his donors cash in, working families are paying more just to get by. With midterms less than a month away, MAGA Inc. and its spinoff super PACs have reserved $160 million in ads to elect Trump's handpicked candidates, paid for by the same people cashing in on his administration. Trump's big-dollar donors want to believe elections belong to whoever writes the biggest check. They're wrong. They have money. We have people. When we take back control of Congress, we can put real checks on Trump, pass laws to crack down on this kind of self-dealing, and build an America that works for everyone, not just the people who can buy a seat at Trump's gold-plated table. I won't stop fighting until we root out this corruption. Thanks for being a part of this, Elizabeth | **Elizabeth Warren is fighting to get Big Money out of politics to make our government work for working families, not just the rich and powerful. And we're doing it with small-dollar, grassroots supporters — not by catering to billionaires or corporations.**

clean_body: How Trump and his administration are benefiting from MAGA donors | | | Want a government job? Need the regulators off your back? Hoping an investigation into your company quietly goes away? In Donald Trump's Washington, there's a way. Write a big check to MAGA Inc., the super PAC he calls: "My money that I control." Researchers at the Center for American Progress Action Fund just followed the money, and MAGA Inc. has raised $404.6 million from donors writing checks of $100,000 or more. Of that $404.6 million, 79% came from just 108 donors who got a documented potential benefit from Trump or his administration Simply put: The people bankrolling Trump's super PAC are the same people profiting from his presidency. Here's what that looks like in reality: Twenty donors tied to government appointments, for themselves or their relatives and business partners, gave $87.75 million. Fifty-seven donors who benefited from regulatory rollbacks gave nearly $82 million. Seven donors who saw enforcement actions against them dropped or reversed gave $78.6 million. Six donors who've pulled in more than $11 billion in federal contracts, including private prison giant GEO Group, gave $41.7 million. Two donors connected to presidential pardons gave $4.5 million. The single biggest industry writing checks? Crypto, at $88.2 million. Add it all up, and you get pay-to-play on a scale we've never seen. Trump promised to drain the swamp. Instead, he handed it a menu. And while his donors cash in, working families are paying more just to get by. With midterms less than a month away, MAGA Inc. and its spinoff super PACs have reserved $160 million in ads to elect Trump's handpicked candidates, paid for by the same people cashing in on his administration. Trump's big-dollar donors want to believe elections belong to whoever writes the biggest check. They're wrong. They have money. We have people. When we take back control of Congress, we can put real checks on Trump, pass laws to crack down on this kind of self-dealing, and build an America that works for everyone, not just the people who can buy a seat at Trump's gold-plated table. I won't stop fighting until we root out this corruption. Thanks for being a part of this, Elizabeth | Elizabeth Warren is fighting to get Big Money out of politics to make our government work for working families, not just the rich and powerful. # Four Weeks Until the Election!
---
| |
The Democrat Congressional Campaign Committee just put Washington’s 5th District on its target list and called this race “in play.” That is Washington, D.C., money lining up behind my opponent. We have four weeks to show them it is not in play, and that starts with your vote!
I fought off out-of-state groups in the primary, and I will do it again, because this seat belongs to Eastern Washington, not to national party bosses. We need to stop federal taxes from stacking on top of what Olympia already charges, protect our dams, and keep fighting for fair trade for our farmers and manufacturers.
Your ballot will arrive by October 16th. Confirm your address with [VoteWA.gov](https://us.list-manage.com/12jl1FYuWAo?e=5a45b9550e&c2id=b2f1dd870633a757190c0f1edbcab238) now, then return your ballot as soon as it shows up! Let’s win this!
---
|
---
| |
# Join Me at the NAACP Candidate Forum
---
[|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/bxUo_V_Uh64?e=5a45b9550e&c2id=b2f1dd870633a757190c0f1edbcab238)
| | Click on the picture to reserve your spot today!
---
| | Join me Wednesday, October 14, from 6 to 8 p.m. at the downtown Spokane Public Library, 906 W Main Ave, for the NAACP Spokane Branch Congressional Forum. Ballots drop October 16th! This is one of the last chances for Eastern Washington voters to hear, in person, where I stand and why I am fighting for our jobs, our farms, our families, and our communities. We would love to see you there!
Mark your calendar, tell a friend, and join us at 6 p.m! Admission is free, reserve your ticket by clicking the picture above.
---
|
---
| |
# Night with the Sports Greats
---
|
---
| | Last week we had a great Night With The Sports Greats event with WSU legend Jack Thompson and Gonzaga great Rob Sacre. It was exactly the kind of evening this campaign was built on. The room was full of people who love this district, love their teams, and still make time to show up. Thank you to our wonderful hosts, to our special guests for sharing their time, and to all those who joined us in support.
---
|
---
|
---
| |
# West Plains Chamber of Commerce Candidate Forum
---
|
---
| | My team enjoyed joining the West Plains Chamber of Commerce for their Candidate Forum last week. Senator Mike Padden was kind enough to speak on my behalf. I appreciated him sharing with local businesses and neighbors about the work we are doing for Eastern Washington. From Fairchild and the West Plains economy to the concerns of local employers and families, I fight for you. Thank you to Sen. Padden and to the West Plains Chamber for organizing this great event.
---
|
---
|
---
| |
# An Evening in Dayton,
# Lincoln Dinner
---
|

Everyone should be able to see it, share it, and understand what's happening. And every subscription helps us reach further, build something lasting, and keep these urgent conversations alive. _Already a paid subscriber? Then like, share, and keep showing up in the comments. It matters more than you know._
* * *
The extradition papers for Andrew and Tristan Tate finally dropped, and the accusations against the manosphere influencers with deep ties to Donald Trump's family and administration are horrifying.
These men are human traffickers. They are child porn peddlers. They are abusers of women and kids. The accusations include sexually abusing animals, sexually abusing minors, selling sexually explicit material of minors over WhatsApp, and a long list of other heinous crimes. They should be locked away for a very long time.
It's unbelievable to me that after a decade of this, these two still haven't been thrown in jail. But it shows exactly how the current system works for people with money and power: if you're wealthy enough, connected enough, and influential enough with the right group of people, you can keep outrunning justice and can get away with it. The Tate brothers were taken into custody by U.S. Marshals in July, and more than two months later, they're _still_ _here_ desperately trying to rattle their way out of facing extradition to the UK.
We've seen it with the Tate brothers. We've seen it with Epstein. Epstein was investigated in 2005, only to weasel his way into a sweetheart plea deal and secret non-prosecution agreement that protected him and his co-conspirators -- buying him another _decade_ to traffic and abuse and maybe even kill children before federal prosecutors finally came after him again. An entire decade. And to this day, we still don't even publicly know the identities of everyone who was protected. We saw it with the Wall Street financial crimes of 2008. We've seen it time and time again.
Power buys access. Access buys protection. And protection buys time. Hell, on any given day I wouldn't be surprised if Donald Trump decided to pardon Diddy or Russell Brand or Harvey Weinstein, given how many horrible people he's already let loose by abusing the pardon power the Constitution gives him.
It's maddening. So I'm writing today to repeat my call: every member of Donald Trump's family, every member of his administration, and every Republican influencer, member of Congress, and staffer who manipulated our criminal justice and political systems to give the Tate brothers sanctuary in the United States, so they could shield themselves from the crimes they're accused of in Europe and elsewhere, should be thoroughly investigated by Congress.
That includes Trump's kids, like Don Jr. and Barron. And these relationships go back years. Tate was messaging with Don Jr. and bragging about having access to the president's son long before Trump returned to office. Barron in particular has a close relationship with Andrew Tate, who he took dating advice from. During the 2024 campaign, one of Tate's closest associates got into Mar-a-Lago and helped cultivate a relationship between Tate and Barron. It includes administration officials like Paul Ingrassia, who had to withdraw a Senate-confirmable nomination after text messages surfaced in which he talked about having a Nazi streak. It includes Alina Habba, who went on Benny Johnson's podcast with Andrew Tate and told him, "I'm a big fan," "I admire what you're doing," and, incredibly, "If you're in the States, I got your back". These are people with proximity to power: to the president and the United States government.
And Tate himself seemed to understand exactly what those relationships could mean for him. While he was still stuck in Romania, he posted after Trump's return to power: "The Tates will be free, Trump is the president." Two weeks later, Romania lifted the brothers' travel ban and they flew to the United States.
I want to know the depth of the depravity that made these people think it was appropriate to bring these scumbags to the United States. I want to know how the Tates got one of MAGA's most infamous lawyers to go work for them. And I want to know what role Mar-a-Lago has played in all of this, because these connections keep leading back there. Joe McBride, the Tates' longtime lawyer and a scumbag in his own right, was at Mar-a-Lago when Trump _launched_ his 2024 presidential campaign. Think about that.
And I want to know just how close they've come to being saved from extradition, McBride has been actively lobbying on their behalf, going _back_ to Mar-a-Lago, meeting with Trump administration officials, and desperately trying to get Donald Trump, Marco Rubio, or somebody else in that family or administration to stop the Tate brothers from being extradited to the UK to finally face their crimes.
If this isn't an attempt to influence and corrupt the government of the United States, I don't know what is.
So far, as far as I can tell, Todd Blanche and the Trump DOJ have done the right thing in the extradition process. They fought the brothers' bail. They're moving forward, however slowly.
